docs.title: Any Texts Statistics (anyTS)
docs.text: anyTS is the language-independent core of the text statistics libraries ruTS (Russian) and esTS (Spanish). It holds the code that does not depend on a language, so that it is written, tested and documented once; a language library adds its tokenizer, lemmatizer, spaCy model and rules and re-exports the core under its own names.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• extract sentences, words and character N-grams with extractors whose tokenizer, lemmatizer and number pattern are hooks a language library overrides
  • give the statistics of every class through one interface: a dictionary, nested or flat, a pandas frame, a printed table and the reading of a statistic by its scale
  • count the basic statistics of a text - sentences, words, syllables, letters and punctuation marks by type - with the syllables of a language library
  • compute the readability metrics of a text - Flesch reading ease, Flesch-Kincaid, Coleman-Liau, ARI, SMOG, Gunning fog, LIX, RIX, Legibilidad µ, the consensus grade and the reading time - with the coefficients of a language library
  • compute lexical diversity metrics (Type-Token Ratio and its variants, MATTR, MSTTR, MTLD, MA-MTLD, MTLD-W, HD-D, the indices of Simpson and Yule, entropy, the laws of Zipf and Heaps), over the whole text or over windows with confidence intervals
  • measure the lexical sophistication of a text by a frequency dictionary in the manner of TAALES: coverage, mean frequency, range and dispersion, surprisal and perplexity, frequency bands and lexical density
  • compute the style metrics - the SEO metrics (nausea, water, spam, naturalness by Zipf's law, keyword density) and the markers of the officialese - with the lists and the morphology of a language library
  • measure the cohesion between sentences in the manner of Coh-Metrix - the overlap of nouns, arguments and content words, adjacent and over all pairs, Dice, givenness, the repetition of the tense and the aspect - and find the connectors of a dictionary with the context rules of a language, with the words and the features of a language library
  • compute the syntactic statistics of the dependency tree - dependency distances, tree depth, valency, coordination chains, clauses, modifiers of a noun, participial clauses, the passive, negations and split predicates - with the clauses and the constructions of a language library, on tree helpers that read the labels shared by Universal Dependencies and ClearNLP and the verb form of a predicate by its auxiliaries
  • compute the phonetic statistics of a text - classes of the sounds, consonant clusters, hiatuses, entropy of the CV patterns, alliteration and assonance by the repetition index, open syllables - with the transcription and the syllables of a language library
  • compare corpora with the measures of corpus linguistics: keywords against a corpus or a frequency dictionary, collocations, the dispersion of a word, stylometry (Burrows's Delta and its variants, Zeta, Kilgarriff's chi-square, the Mendenhall curve), the comparison of corpora feature by feature with effect sizes, a bootstrap by texts and the Holm correction, and a KWIC concordance
  • plot Zipf's law, vocabulary growth, sentence lengths, literature fingerprinting, a word tree, corpus and stylometric measures, with the labels of the plots as a parameter, and highlight a text by the layers of a language library
  • build components of spaCy pipelines that put the statistics into an extension of Doc
  • build datasets: download an archive with a checksum, extract it safely and filter the records
  • catch errors of one hierarchy whose classes are also built-in exceptions

The reference of every function is a named section that the libraries include in their own documentation, so a formula is described in one place.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.11 or newer.

pip install anyts

The dependencies are on the Installation page.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
>>> from anyts import DiversityStats, SentsExtractor, WordsExtractor

>>> text = "The cat sat on the mat. The dog sat on the log! The cat and the dog slept."

>>> SentsExtractor().extract(text)
('The cat sat on the mat.', 'The dog sat on the log!', 'The cat and the dog slept.')

>>> ds = DiversityStats(WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract(text))
>>> ds.ttr, round(ds.entropy, 3)
(0.5, 2.864)

A language library subclasses the extractors and overrides their hooks:

>>> class Words(WordsExtractor):
...     def lemmatize(self, word):
...         return {"sat": "sit", "slept": "sleep"}.get(word.lower(), word)

>>> Words(lowercase=True, use_lexemes=True).extract("The cat sat. The dog slept.")
('the', 'cat', 'sit', 'the', 'dog', 'sleep')

The corpus measures take lists of words:

>>> from anyts.corpus import keyness

>>> cats = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract("The cat sat on the mat. The cat saw a bird. The cat slept.")
>>> dogs = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract("The dog sat on the log. The dog saw a cat. The dog barked.")
>>> [(keyword.word, round(keyword.log_ratio, 2)) for keyword in keyness(cats, dogs, min_freq=2)]
[('cat', 1.58)]

docs.title: Components
docs.text: anyts.components.StatsComponent, anyts.components.BasicStatsComponent and the components of the other classes of statistics

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The base of the components of spaCy that put the statistics of a text into an extension of Doc: a component registers the extension when added to a pipeline and puts the statistics of every document into doc._.<name>. Writing components in general is described in the documentation of spaCy.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text:
A language library subclasses StatsComponent for every class of its statistics and registers the subclass as a factory under its prefix, Language.factory("<prefix>_<statistics>"), so that the factories of several libraries live in one process; declared as entry points of spacy_factories, they load with spacy.load without importing the library. The subclass sets the class of its statistics and checks its parameters in its __init__ before calling the __init__ of the base, so a wrong parameter fails at add_pipe. The components of the classes of statistics of the core already carry their parameters and checks; a library sets its subclass of the statistics on them.

Hook Description stats_class Class attribute: the class of statistics made of a document, None by default; a component with neither a concrete class nor its own compute raises ParameterError at add_pipe stats_params Class attribute: the attributes of the component passed to the class of statistics as keyword arguments, none by default; a name the component lacks raises ParameterError at add_pipe compute(doc) The statistics of a document, stats_class(doc, **params) by default; overridden by a component that computes otherwise, such as one reusing the statistics of another component prepare(nlp) Preparing the pipeline when the component is added, such as the rules of the tokenizer; nothing by default accepts(doc) Whether a document gets the statistics; by default whether it has a word (has_words) messages Class attribute: the messages of the errors by key, MESSAGES by default from_extension(doc, name, stats_class, factory=None) The statistics another component put into the document, for reuse instead of computing them again; an extension without statistics of the class raises SourceError, which names the factory to add. The other component must accept every document the reusing one does, since a document it passes leaves None

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
The name of the pipe is the name of the extension: nlp.add_pipe(factory, name="basic") puts the statistics into doc._.basic. Without name both take the name of the factory. The extension follows the pipe when the pipeline renames it (nlp.rename_pipe). A name taken by an extension of another package raises ParameterError instead of replacing it: at add_pipe, or at the first document after rename_pipe, which renames the pipe before the component learns its name. A component taken from another pipeline (add_pipe(name, source=other)) is the same object in both, so under a new name it writes to that extension in the other pipeline too; a separate component comes from the factory, add_pipe(factory, name=...). The same component can be added twice under different names, with different parameters. A document with no words - an empty string, whitespace, punctuation alone - passes through a component untouched, its extension left at None.

Serialization

A component keeps an object of statistics in doc._.<name>, and spaCy cannot serialize it: Doc.to_bytes(), DocBin(store_user_data=True) and nlp.pipe(..., n_process>1) fail with these components in the pipeline. To save a document, leave the user data out (doc.to_bytes(exclude=["user_data"])) or keep doc._.<name>.get_stats() separately; for multiprocessing compute the statistics in the main process after nlp.pipe, without the components.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description nlp Language - Pipeline the component is added to name str - Name of the component in the pipeline and of the extension

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
A component of the lexical diversity of the words of a Doc.

Example

import spacy
from spacy.language import Language

from anyts import DiversityStats
from anyts.components import StatsComponent
from anyts.diversity_stats import check_params
from anyts.utils import iter_doc_words


class Diversity(DiversityStats):
    def __init__(self, doc, window_len=50):
        words = [word.lower() for _, _, word in iter_doc_words(doc)]
        super().__init__(words, window_len=window_len)


@Language.factory("demo_diversity")
class DiversityComponent(StatsComponent):
    stats_class = Diversity
    stats_params = ("window_len",)

    def __init__(self, nlp, name, window_len=50):
        check_params(window_len=window_len, messages=self.messages)
        self.window_len = window_len
        super().__init__(nlp, name)


nlp = spacy.blank("xx")
nlp.add_pipe("demo_diversity", name="diversity", config={"window_len": 3})
nlp("The cat and the dog")._.diversity.ttr
# 0.8
nlp("?!")._.diversity
# None

docs.title: Components of the classes of statistics
docs.text:
Each class of statistics of the core has a component that takes its parameters in the config of the pipe, checks them at add_pipe and passes them to the class; a language library subclasses it, sets its subclass of the statistics as stats_class and registers it under its prefix:

@Language.factory("<prefix>_phon")
class PhonStatsComponent(anyts.components.PhonStatsComponent):
    stats_class = PhonStats  # the subclass of the library

The class of the core is the default of stats_class. Where it cannot read a Doc - an abstract class (BasicStats, LexicalStats, PhonStats), ReadabilityStats without the basic_stats_class of a library, none at all (DiversityStatsComponent, the class of the core taking a list of words) - the component cannot be added until the library gives its class.

Component Class of statistics Parameters BasicStatsComponent BasicStats - ReadabilityStatsComponent ReadabilityStats preset, basic DiversityStatsComponent set by a library window_len, mtld_threshold, mtld_min_len, hdd_sample_size, log_base LexicalStatsComponent LexicalStats - StyleStatsComponent StyleStats stopwords, top_n, nausea_stopwords PhonStatsComponent PhonStats window_len SyntaxStatsComponent SyntaxStats - CohesionStatsComponent CohesionStats -

BasicStatsComponent puts the basic statistics of a document into its extension.

ReadabilityStatsComponent puts the readability metrics into the extension, computed from the document or, with basic, from the basic statistics another component put into it. A library sets basic_factory, the factory of its component of the basic statistics, which the error names when that extension holds none.

Parameter Type Default Description preset str None Preset of the coefficients, one of the presets of the class; the default of the class if None basic str None Extension of a component of the basic statistics to reuse instead of computing them again

With preset left at None the config of a saved pipeline holds no preset, and the pipeline takes the default of the class when it is loaded; a library that wants its default written into the config gives it in the signature of its subclass. A preset that is not a string or not one of the class and an extension not named by a string raise ParameterError, a class without basic_stats_class and no basic SourceTypeError.

DiversityStatsComponent puts the lexical diversity metrics into the extension, by a class of the library that reads a Doc. Its parameters are those of DiversityStats - window_len, mtld_threshold, mtld_min_len, hdd_sample_size, log_base - with the same defaults, and a wrong one raises ParameterError (check_params of the diversity).

LexicalStatsComponent puts the lexical sophistication statistics into the extension, with the frequency dictionary of its attribute freq_dict: None by default, for the dictionary of the class, and set by a library in the constructor of its component. A document gets the statistics when it has a word of iter_doc_words (with join_hyphens) other than a number of the method is_number, anyts.utils.is_number by default; a library gives the numbers its class leaves out, so a document of numbers alone passes untouched.

StyleStatsComponent puts the style metrics into the extension.

Parameter Type Default Description stopwords list[str] None Stopwords of the water content; those of the class if None top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words of the academic nausea and of the naturalness by Zipf's law (NAUSEA_TOP_N) nausea_stopwords list[str] None Words left out of the most frequent words of the academic nausea; those of the class if None

Stopwords that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, a top_n that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

PhonStatsComponent puts the phonetic statistics into the extension; window_len (by default PHON_WINDOW_LEN, 3) is the window in words of the alliteration and the assonance, and one that is not an integer of at least 2 raises ParameterError.

SyntaxStatsComponent puts the syntactic statistics into the extension; they need a parser before it.

CohesionStatsComponent puts the cohesion statistics into the extension; by default they need the parts of speech and the lemmas before it.

docs.title: start_sents_after_blank_lines
docs.text:
anyts.components.start_sents_after_blank_lines

A component that starts a sentence at the first token after a blank line - a line break, optional whitespace and another line break - so that a heading, a list item or a paragraph without a final mark is a sentence of its own, as in the sentence extractor. It goes before the parser, senter or sentencizer, which keeps its starts and places the others. The whitespace before such a start stays with the sentence before it, and the marks that open a paragraph (a dash of a dialogue, ¡, «) stay with its first word. Alone, the component leaves the sentences within a paragraph unsplit and sets partial boundaries (has_sents), so the statistics take the sentences of such a document from its text. A parsed document, such as one passed through the pipeline again, passes untouched, since spaCy keeps its sentences. A language library registers the component under its prefix, Language.component("<prefix>_blank_lines", func=start_sents_after_blank_lines).

Parameter Type Default Description doc Doc - Doc object

Example

import spacy
from spacy.language import Language

from anyts.components import start_sents_after_blank_lines

Language.component("demo_blank_lines", func=start_sents_after_blank_lines)
nlp = spacy.blank("xx")
nlp.add_pipe("demo_blank_lines")
nlp.add_pipe("sentencizer")
[sent.text.strip() for sent in nlp("What is new\n\nFaster import. Fewer bugs.").sents]
# ['What is new', 'Faster import.', 'Fewer bugs.']

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
anyts.datasets

The base of a dataset and the functions that download, verify and extract its archive and filter its records.

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text:
An abstract dataset: a name, a dictionary of reference information meta and the methods a dataset implements - iteration over the records, check_data, get_texts, get_records and download(force=False). repr gives the name of the class and the name of the dataset, <repr_name>('<name>'), and the property info is the name under the key name_key followed by meta.

Parameter Type Default Description name str - Name of the dataset meta dict None Reference information about the dataset

The class attributes repr_name and name_key are the name of the class in repr and the key of the name in info; a subclass overrides them.

In the core repr_name is "Dataset" and name_key is "name".

docs.title: fetch_archive
docs.text:
Downloads the archive of a dataset; when it is just downloaded or missing says the extracted files are not all in place, verifies it and extracts the files. The SHA-256 checksum may be in upper or lower case; an archive that fails it is removed and downloaded again once, and a second failure raises DownloadError. The files are extracted aside, next to the archive, and replace the directory of the dataset (or a link in its place) only once complete, the earlier directory removed only once they are in place: an interrupted extraction or a failed replacement leaves the earlier files intact, and concurrent calls do not share partial files. The name of the archive needs an extension, since the directory is named after the archive without it; otherwise ParameterError is raised before the download.

Parameter Type Default Description url str - Address of the archive filepath str/Path - Path to the archive; the files are extracted into its directory, under the name of the archive without its extensions checksum str - SHA-256 checksum of the archive missing bool - Whether the extracted files are missing force bool False Download the archive even if it is already there user_agent str USER_AGENT User-Agent header of the request, the name of the library

docs.title: download_file
docs.text:
Downloads a file into a directory and returns its path, or an empty string if the file is already there and force is off. The name of the file is the decoded last part of the path of the address; an address without one needs filename, and a name with a drive or a separator raises DownloadError. The file is written under a temporary name and renamed once complete: a broken, interrupted or cut download (shorter than the announced length) raises DownloadError and leaves no partial file, and concurrent downloads do not share partial files. The server is waited for at most DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT (60) seconds.

Parameter Type Default Description url str - Address of the file dirpath str/Path - Directory for the downloaded file filename str None Name of the downloaded file; the last part of the address by default force bool False Download the file even if it is already there user_agent str USER_AGENT User-Agent header of the request, the name of the library

In the core USER_AGENT is "anyTS"; a language library passes its own name.

docs.title: extract_archive
docs.text:
Extracts a ZIP or TAR archive and returns the directory with the files. Paths leading outside the directory (absolute, with a drive or a network share, or with ..) and links are refused before anything is written, on any version of Python. The archive is extracted aside and put in place once complete: a single root directory takes the name of the archive without its extensions (corpus_v1.tar.xz - corpus_v1), replacing an earlier extraction; otherwise the files go into the directory, replacing those of the same names and keeping the others. A file in the place of a directory or the other way round is refused before anything is replaced. A missing file, a file that is not an archive, a corrupted or empty archive, a directory that cannot be created and files that cannot be replaced raise DataFileError, and a path that is neither a string nor a Path SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description archive_file str/Path - Path to the archive extract_dir str/Path None Directory for the extracted files; the directory of the archive by default

docs.title: sha256
docs.text:
Computes the SHA-256 checksum of a file as a hexadecimal string in lower case; a missing file gives an empty string, and a path that is neither a string nor a Path raises SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description path str/Path - Path to the file

docs.title: to_path
docs.text:
Converts a string or a Path into a Path, expanding a leading ~ into the home directory; any other value raises SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description path str/Path - Path as a string or a Path

docs.title: Filters of the records
docs.text:
check_limit(limit) checks the number of records to take: None or a non-negative integer, otherwise ParameterError.

length_filters(min_len, max_len) returns the predicates that keep the records whose field text is at least min_len and at most max_len characters long; None sets no bound. A bound that is not an integer or is below one, or a minimum greater than the maximum, raises ParameterError.

substring_filter(field, value, fold) returns the predicate that keeps the records whose field holds the substring value. Both are folded by fold, so the differences of case and diacritics a language ignores do not count. The substring is plain text, not a regular expression; a field that is not a string does not match. A value that is not a string raises ParameterError, and a fold that cannot be called SourceTypeError.

In the core fold is fold_diacritics.

fold_diacritics(value) lower-cases a string (str.casefold), decomposes it (NFD) and drops the combining marks, so Galdós and galdos are the same. A letter that Unicode decomposes into a base letter and a mark is folded too (й gives и); a language where such a letter is a letter of its own passes another fold.

Example

from anyts.datasets import fold_diacritics, length_filters, substring_filter

records = [
    {"author": "Benito Pérez Galdós", "text": "A long text of the novel"},
    {"author": "Rubén Darío", "text": "A poem"},
]
filters = [substring_filter("author", "galdos"), *length_filters(10, None)]
[record["author"] for record in records if all(f(record) for f in filters)]
# ['Benito Pérez Galdós']
fold_diacritics("Pérez Galdós")
# 'perez galdos'

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
anyts.exceptions

All exceptions of the library inherit the base class AnyTSError and a built-in Python class, and can be caught by either.

Exception Built-in class When raised AnyTSError Exception Base class, never raised itself SourceTypeError TypeError An argument is of an unsupported type: the source or the text, a text where a list is expected, an extractor, basic statistics of another class, a path, a hook that is not callable (a tokenizer, a lemmatizer, a measure), or a tokenizer, a sentence splitter or the parse, analyze, syllabify, transcribe or find of a class that returns what the core cannot use SourceError ValueError The source has no words, sentences or texts to compute a statistic on, lacks an annotation the statistic needs, or holds values it cannot take: a negative or infinite frequency, a matrix of distances that is not one ParameterError ValueError A parameter is out of range or not a finite number, a name (of a measure, a variant, a preset, a layer, a norm) is unknown, the labels or the axes of a plot are set incorrectly, or a layer of the highlighting asks for an annotation the source lacks UnknownStatError ParameterError, KeyError An unknown statistic is requested by name DatasetNotFoundError OSError The spaCy model is not installed or a dataset is not downloaded; the message gives the command that fixes it DataFileError ValueError The archive of a dataset cannot be extracted or is unsafe, or a line of a dataset file cannot be read DownloadError RuntimeError A file cannot be downloaded, is cut short or fails the checksum verification, its name is not a plain name, or its directory cannot be created

The classes are available from anyts and from anyts.exceptions. A language library re-exports them under its own names as aliases, not subclasses, so its base class catches the errors of the core too.

Example

from anyts import AnyTSError, ParameterError, WordsExtractor

try:
    WordsExtractor(ngram_range=(2, 1))
except ParameterError as e:
    print(e)
# The lower N-gram bound is greater than the upper

try:
    WordsExtractor(tokenizer=42).extract("The cat sleeps.")
except AnyTSError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__)
# SourceTypeError

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
The errors of the classes of statistics (Stats and its subclasses), of StatsComponent, of the extractors SentsExtractor, WordsExtractor and CharNgramsExtractor and of ConnectorMatcher take their messages from the class attribute messages, a mapping of a key to a message, anyts.constants.MESSAGES in English by default; the messages with fields in braces are format strings. A language library sets the messages of its language on its subclasses, messages = {**MESSAGES, **own}, and they cover every error such a class raises itself. The functions check_params, calc_windowed and calc_reading_time, which these classes call, take the messages as the keyword messages.

The shared checks of anyts.utils (check_integer, check_number, check_words, check_sequence), which these classes call too, and the other functions of the core keep their messages in English.

Example

from anyts.constants import MESSAGES
from anyts.diversity_stats import DiversityStats


class Diversity(DiversityStats):
    messages = {**MESSAGES, "no_words": "Il testo non contiene parole"}


try:
    Diversity([])
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)
# Il testo non contiene parole

docs.title: Collocations
docs.text: anyts.corpus.collocations(), anyts.corpus.Collocation

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Collocation extraction - pairs of words that occur together more often than independence would give: fixed expressions, terminology, the combinatorics of a word. The measures of association are those of Sketch Engine and of nltk.metrics.association.

Pairs are ordered, as in NLTK: the right word occurs at most window words after the left one, each pair of positions counted once; window=1 gives bigrams. The measures take the pair frequency divided by the window (Church and Hanks 1990, as in NLTK), which keeps the expected frequency independent of the window and Dice and the minimum sensitivity at most one; freq_pair stays undivided. So with window > 1 an always adjacent pair gets a logDice of \(14 - \log_2 window\) (13 at a window of 2), not 14 as in Sketch Engine with its raw co-occurrence; 14 needs a pair at every distance within the window. node keeps the pairs with the given word on either side.

Words are compared as they are: case, lemmatization and stop words belong to the word extractor; lemmas suit fixed expressions, word forms suit grammatical constructions.

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
For a pair of words of frequencies \(f_a\) and \(f_b\), a pair frequency \(f_{ab}\) and a number of words \(N\):

Measure Key Formula Description Mutual information mi \(\log_2 \frac{f_{ab} N}{f_a f_b}\) Church and Hanks (1990); overrates rare pairs MI³ mi3 \(\log_2 \frac{f_{ab}^3 N}{f_a f_b}\) Oakes (1998); favours frequent pairs t-score t_score \(\frac{f_{ab} - f_a f_b / N}{\sqrt{f_{ab}}}\) Church et al. (1991); favours frequent pairs Dice coefficient dice \(\frac{2 f_{ab}}{f_a + f_b}\) does not depend on the size of the text logDice logdice \(14 + \log_2 \frac{2 f_{ab}}{f_a + f_b}\) Rychlý (2008); does not depend on the size of the text, at most 14, below zero - a weak link; the default measure, as in Sketch Engine Log-likelihood log_likelihood \(G^2 = 2 \sum O \ln \frac{O}{E}\) Dunning (1993); over the 2×2 contingency table, nan if one of the words fills the whole text NPMI npmi \(\frac{MI}{-\log_2 (f_{ab} / N)}\) Bouma (2009); from −1 to 1, one means the words occur only together Minimum sensitivity min_sensitivity \(\min(\frac{f_{ab}}{f_a}, \frac{f_{ab}}{f_b})\) Pedersen (1998); from 0 to 1

The module anyts.corpus.collocations gives them as the functions calc_mi, calc_mi3, calc_t_score, calc_dice, calc_logdice, calc_log_likelihood, calc_npmi and calc_min_sensitivity of (freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n); their names and descriptions are in anyts.constants.COLLOCATION_MEASURES.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order window int 5 Greatest distance between the words of a pair measure str logdice Measure of anyts.constants.COLLOCATION_MEASURES min_freq int 2 Minimum frequency of a pair node str None Word whose combinatorics is needed; None - every pair top_n int None Number of collocations; None - all of them

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and no words SourceError. An unknown measure, a window or a top_n that is not an integer of at least one, a min_freq that is not an integer and a node that is not a string raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
A list of Collocation named tuples by descending measure and frequency of the pair (ties broken alphabetically); pd.DataFrame(found) gives a table.

Field Type Description left str Left word right str Right word, occurring within the window after the left one freq_left int Frequency of the left word freq_right int Frequency of the right word freq_pair int Frequency of the co-occurrence score float Value of the chosen measure

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Example

from anyts import WordsExtractor
from anyts.corpus import collocations

words = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract(
    "The cat was at the window and watched the birds. The birds flew away and the cat "
    "fell asleep at the window. Tomorrow the cat will be at the window and watch the birds."
)

collocations(words, window=2, top_n=1)
# [Collocation(left='at', right='window', freq_left=3, freq_right=3, freq_pair=3, score=13.0)]

[
    (c.left, c.right, round(c.score, 2))
    for c in collocations(words, window=1, node="cat", min_freq=1, measure="mi")[:2]
]
# [('cat', 'fell', 3.5), ('cat', 'was', 3.5)]

docs.title: Corpus comparison
docs.text: anyts.corpus.compare_features(), anyts.corpus.check_comparison_params(), anyts.corpus.compare_values(), anyts.corpus.calc_cohen_d(), anyts.corpus.calc_cliff_delta(), anyts.corpus.bootstrap_median_diff(), anyts.corpus.holm_correction(), anyts.corpus.split_windows(), anyts.corpus.sentence_rhythm()

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Comparing two corpora feature by feature. Each corpus is a table of the features of its windows, parts of the texts of about equal size, so the features do not depend on text length. compare_features(table_a, table_b, labels, n_bootstrap, seed) gives one row per column, by descending absolute Cliff's delta, the features without statistics last. The bootstrap resamples whole texts by the index level text; without it every row is a text of its own. A column missing from one table gives nan.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
For a feature with the values \(x_1 \dots x_{n_A}\) in corpus A and \(y_1 \dots y_{n_B}\) in corpus B (undefined and infinite values dropped; with fewer than two values on a side - nan):

Column Description mean_A, mean_B, median_A, median_B means and medians median_diff, ci_low, ci_high the difference of the medians and its 95% percentile bootstrap interval: both sets are resampled n_bootstrap times (bootstrap_median_diff) cohen_d \(d = (\bar{x} - \bar{y}) / s\), \(s\) - the pooled standard deviation; 0.2 - a small effect, 0.5 - medium, 0.8 - large (calc_cohen_d) cliff_delta \(\delta = P(x > y) - P(x < y)\) from −1 to 1; \(\lvert\delta\rvert\) < 0.147 - a negligible effect, < 0.33 - small, < 0.474 - medium, large otherwise (Romano et al. 2006; calc_cliff_delta) auc the feature as a classifier: the share of the pairs of windows with the value in A greater than in B, ties counted as half; \(\delta = 2 \cdot AUC - 1\), 0.5 - the feature does not tell the corpora apart u, p_value the Mann-Whitney U statistic and the two-sided p-value (scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu) p_holm the p-value with Holm's correction for the number of features (holm_correction) n_A, n_B number of windows with a defined value n_texts_A, n_texts_B number of texts behind those windows

The columns are anyts.corpus.COMPARISON_COLUMNS with A and B replaced by the labels of the corpora. Cliff's delta and the AUC come from the same U statistic and agree; Cohen's d is sensitive to outliers and non-normality, so it is best read next to the delta.

Windows of one text are not independent

The test and the effect sizes take the windows for independent observations, which the windows of one text are not: with few texts the p-values are too small and reflect the chosen texts as much as the corpora. The bootstrap resamples whole texts (a cluster bootstrap), so its interval covers the spread between texts; it needs at least two texts on each side and is rough with few.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description table_a DataFrame - Features of the windows of the first corpus, one row per window table_b DataFrame - Features of the windows of the second corpus labels tuple[str, str] ("A", "B") Names of the corpora for the columns, two strings that give distinct columns n_bootstrap int 1000 Number of bootstrap samples seed int/Generator 0 Seed of the random number generator, a non-negative integer, or a numpy Generator; None - a random one

A table that is not a DataFrame, repeats the name of a column or has a column that is not numeric raises SourceTypeError; the other parameters are checked by check_comparison_params.

check_comparison_params(labels=("A", "B"), n_bootstrap=1000, seed=0) checks the parameters of compare_features before the texts are processed: it raises ParameterError unless the labels are two strings that give distinct columns (("diff", "B") would repeat median_diff), the number of bootstrap samples is an integer of at least one and the seed is None, a non-negative integer or a numpy Generator.

Example

import pandas as pd

from anyts.corpus import compare_features

short = pd.DataFrame({"length": [14.0, 15.0, 13.0, 16.0]})
long = pd.DataFrame({"length": [33.0, 35.0, 31.0, 29.0]})
result = compare_features(short, long, labels=("short", "long"), n_bootstrap=200)
result.loc[
    "length", ["mean_short", "mean_long", "median_diff", "ci_low", "ci_high", "cliff_delta"]
].tolist()
# [14.5, 32.0, -17.5, -20.5, -14.5, -1.0]

docs.title: Functions of the statistics
docs.text:
compare_values(values_a, values_b, n_bootstrap=1000, rng=None, texts_a=None, texts_b=None) compares two sets of values of one feature and returns one row in the order of anyts.corpus.COMPARISON_COLUMNS, p_holm left nan. Undefined and infinite values, missing ones (None, NA) included, are dropped with their texts; texts_a and texts_b give the text of every value for the bootstrap. A value that is not a number or a missing one, values that are not a flat list and texts that are not labels of one type raise SourceTypeError; an n_bootstrap that is not an integer of at least one, texts not as many as the values and an rng that is not a numpy Generator raise ParameterError.

calc_cohen_d(values_a, values_b) - Cohen's d with the pooled sample variances (ddof=1); nan with fewer than two values on a side or without spread. A value that is not a number or a missing one (None, NA) and values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError.

calc_cliff_delta(values_a, values_b) - Cliff's delta, the share of the pairs where the first value is greater minus the share where it is smaller; nan for an empty set or an undefined value. Computed by sorting, in \(O((n_A + n_B) \log n_B)\) time and linear memory. A value that is not a number or a missing one (None, NA) and values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError.

bootstrap_median_diff(values_a, values_b, n_bootstrap=1000, rng=None, confidence=0.95, texts_a=None, texts_b=None) - the percentile bootstrap interval of the difference of the medians. With texts_a and texts_b whole texts are resampled, the median of a draw taken over the values of its texts; with fewer than two texts on a side the interval is nan. A value that is not a number or a missing one, values that are not a flat list and texts that are not labels of one type raise SourceTypeError; an n_bootstrap that is not an integer of at least one, a confidence that is not a number in (0, 1), texts not as many as the values and an rng that is not a numpy Generator raise ParameterError.

holm_correction(p_values) - Holm's correction for multiple comparisons: the p-values are sorted in ascending order, the i-th is multiplied by (m − i + 1), where m is the number of defined values, then the running maximum is taken and capped at one; nan stays nan. A p-value that is not a number or a missing one and p-values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError, and a p-value outside [0, 1] ParameterError.

Example

from anyts.corpus import calc_cliff_delta, calc_cohen_d, holm_correction

round(calc_cohen_d([2, 4, 6, 8], [1, 3, 5, 7]), 3)
# 0.387
calc_cliff_delta([2, 4, 6, 8], [1, 3, 5, 7])
# 0.25
holm_correction([0.01, 0.04, 0.03]).round(3).tolist()
# [0.03, 0.06, 0.06]

docs.title: Windows of a text
docs.text:
split_windows(text, window, min_words) cuts a text into consecutive windows of exactly window words, so the features that depend on length are comparable between texts. The rest is a window only with at least min_words words (by default a whole window, so it is dropped). A boundary goes before the first word of a window and its opening marks; a symmetric mark, such as a straight quote or the dash of an aside, closes the previous window when glued to its last word or after a closing mark. Windows are stripped of whitespace; window=None gives the whole text. The words and their positions come from tokenize, by default the words of WordsExtractor.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string window int 1000 Size of a window in words; None - the whole text min_words int None Smallest number of words in a window; None - a whole window, or one word without a window tokenize Callable None Words of a text with their start and end positions opening_marks Collection[str] OPENING_MARKS Marks that open a phrase symmetric_marks Collection[str] SYMMETRIC_MARKS Opening marks that close a phrase as well closing_marks Collection[str] CLOSING_MARKS Marks that close a phrase messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

A text that is not a string, a tokenizer that is not callable or does not give the words in order as triples of integer bounds within the text and a string, and marks that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, a window or min_words that is not an integer of at least one, min_words above the window and a mark of more than one character ParameterError. A text without words or shorter than min_words gives an empty list.

The marks of the core are those of anyts.constants: quotes, brackets and dashes open a phrase, the straight quotes and the dashes are symmetric, and the final marks, the comma, the semicolon, the closing brackets, guillemet and quotes close one.

docs.title: Rhythm of the sentences
docs.text:
sentence_rhythm(lengths) gives the rhythm of the sentences from their lengths in words: the mean sents_mean, the standard deviation sents_std, the coefficient of variation sents_cv and the lag-1 autocorrelation of neighbouring lengths sents_autocorr (Yule, 1939). The deviation needs two sentences, the autocorrelation three of unequal lengths, the coefficient of variation a mean above zero; otherwise, and without sentences, a feature is nan. Lengths that are not a list of integers raise SourceTypeError, a negative length ParameterError, with the messages of the keyword messages.

Example

from anyts.corpus import sentence_rhythm, split_windows

split_windows("One two three four five", 2, min_words=1)
# ['One two', 'three four', 'five']
{key: round(value, 3) for key, value in sentence_rhythm([4, 8, 2, 7]).items()}
# {'sents_mean': 5.25, 'sents_std': 2.754, 'sents_cv': 0.525, 'sents_autocorr': -0.794}

docs.title: Word dispersion
docs.text: anyts.corpus.dispersion(), anyts.corpus.Dispersion

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The dispersion of a word is how evenly it is spread over the parts of a text or of a corpus. Frequency does not tell a word occurring once in every chapter from one gathered in a single chapter; the measures of dispersion (Gries 2008, 2020) complement it.

parts is the number of parts of about equal size or the sizes of the parts in order (sentences, paragraphs, chapters, documents of a corpus), adding up to the number of words. Six measures are computed from the frequencies of every word by part; Gries recommends DP as the main one.

Words are compared as they are: case and lemmatization belong to the word extractor.

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
For \(n\) parts of shares \(s_i\) of the text, frequencies of the word by part \(v_i\) and a total frequency \(f = \sum v_i\); \(p_i = v_i / n_i\) is the relative frequency in a part of size \(n_i\):

Measure Field Formula Values Deviation of proportions DP dp \(\frac{1}{2} \sum \left\lvert \frac{v_i}{f} - s_i \right\rvert\) 0 - in proportion to the sizes of the parts, \(1 - s_i\) - all in part \(i\), so at most \(1 - \min s_i\); Gries (2008) Normalized DP dp_norm \(\frac{DP}{1 - \min s_i}\) the maximum is one whatever the split; Lijffijt and Gries (2012) Juilland's D juilland_d \(1 - \frac{V}{\sqrt{n - 1}}\), \(V = \frac{\sigma(p)}{\mu(p)}\) 1 - even, 0 - in one part; Juilland and Chang-Rodríguez (1964), with the population standard deviation \(\sigma\) as in Gries (2020); Gries (2008) takes the sample one Carroll's D2 carroll_d2 \(\frac{H(p)}{\log_2 n}\) entropy of the distribution \(p_i\); 1 - even, 0 - in one part; Carroll (1970) Rosengren's S rosengren_s \(\frac{(\sum \sqrt{s_i v_i})^2}{f}\) 1 - in proportion, tends to \(1/n\) when gathered in one of equal parts; Rosengren (1971) Kullback-Leibler divergence kl_divergence \(\sum \frac{v_i}{f} \log_2 \frac{v_i / f}{s_i}\) in bits; 0 - in proportion, grows when gathered in small parts; Gries (2020)

The module anyts.corpus.dispersion gives them as the functions calc_dp, calc_dp_norm, calc_juilland_d, calc_carroll_d2, calc_rosengren_s and calc_kl_divergence of (frequencies, sizes), the frequencies of the word by part and the sizes of the parts; their names are in anyts.constants.DISPERSION_STATS_DESC. For a word of zero frequency every measure is nan.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order parts int/list[int] 10 Number of parts (from 2 to the number of words) or sizes of the parts word str None Word whose dispersion is needed; None - every word min_freq int 1 Minimum frequency of a word

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and no words SourceError. A parts that is neither an integer from 2 to the number of words nor two or more positive integers adding up to it, a word that is not a string and a min_freq that is not an integer raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A list of Dispersion named tuples by descending frequency: word, freq, dp, dp_norm, juilland_d, carroll_d2, rosengren_s and kl_divergence; pd.DataFrame(result) gives a table.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Example

from anyts import SentsExtractor, WordsExtractor
from anyts.corpus import dispersion

text = (
    "The cat was at the window and watched the birds. The birds flew away and the cat "
    "fell asleep at the window. Tomorrow the cat will be at the window and watch the birds."
)
we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
words = we.extract(text)
sizes = [len(we.extract(sent)) for sent in SentsExtractor().extract(text)]
sizes
# [10, 12, 12]

dispersion(words, parts=sizes, word="cat")
# [Dispersion(word='cat', freq=3, dp=0.039215686274509776, dp_norm=0.05555555555555552,
#  juilland_d=0.9374999999999999, carroll_d2=0.9965119062478288,
#  rosengren_s=0.998213770592287, kl_divergence=0.005215975085958165)]

# Three equal parts: birds are gathered at the edges of the text
[(d.word, round(d.dp, 2)) for d in dispersion(words, parts=3, min_freq=3)]
# [('the', 0.1), ('cat', 0.02), ('at', 0.02), ('window', 0.02), ('and', 0.02), ('birds', 0.32)]

docs.title: Keywords
docs.text: anyts.corpus.keyness(), anyts.corpus.check_keyness_params(), anyts.corpus.Keyword, anyts.corpus.FrequencyReference

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Keyword extraction (keyness) for a target corpus against a reference one: the words that occur significantly more often in the target corpus than in the reference.

Every word gets two values that Gabrielatos and Marchi and Hardie recommend reading together: the log-likelihood \(G^2\) with its p-value (whether there is a difference) and Log Ratio (how large it is), plus the chosen measure score, which sorts the list. The measures of significance (\(G^2\), chi-square, BIC) and ELL, the effect size of \(G^2\), are negative when the word is more frequent in the reference; %DIFF, Log Ratio and the odds ratio are directional by construction.

The reference may be a list of words, a mapping of frequencies (its size is the sum of the counts) or a FrequencyReference. Words are compared as they are: case, lemmatization and stop words belong to the word extractor, and both corpora have to be extracted the same way.

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
For a word of frequency \(a\) in a target corpus of size \(c\) and of frequency \(b\) in a reference corpus of size \(d\), \(N = c + d\):

Measure Key Formula Description Log-likelihood log_likelihood \(G^2 = 2\,(a \ln \frac{a}{E_1} + b \ln \frac{b}{E_2})\), \(E_1 = \frac{c\,(a+b)}{N}\), \(E_2 = \frac{d\,(a+b)}{N}\) Rayson and Garside (2000); critical values anyts.constants.G2_CRITICAL_VALUES: 3.84 for p < 0.05, 6.63 for p < 0.01, 10.83 for p < 0.001, 15.13 for p < 0.0001 Chi-square chi2 \(\chi^2 = \frac{N\,\max(\lvert a(d-b) - b(c-a) \rvert - N/2,\ 0)^2}{(a+b)(N-a-b)\,c\,d}\) with Yates's correction over the 2×2 contingency table; when the correction exceeds the difference, the statistic is zero %DIFF diff \(\frac{NF_a - NF_b}{NF_b} \cdot 100\) Gabrielatos and Marchi (2011); \(NF\) - frequency per million words Log Ratio log_ratio \(\log_2 \frac{NF_a}{NF_b}\) Hardie (2014); one means the word is twice as frequent in the target corpus BIC bic \(\operatorname{sign}(G^2) \cdot (\lvert G^2 \rvert - \ln N)\) Wilson (2013); in absolute value above 2 - positive evidence of a difference, above 6 - strong, above 10 - very strong; a negative value with \(\lvert G^2 \rvert < \ln N\) means no evidence, not the opposite direction ELL ell \(\frac{G^2}{N \ln \min(E_1, E_2)}\) Johnston, Berry and Mielke (2006); effect size of \(G^2\), the share of the greatest possible departure from the expected frequencies, from 0 to 1; nan when the least expected frequency is at most one (a logarithm of zero or below), unbounded just above one Odds ratio odds_ratio \(\frac{a / (c - a)}{b / (d - b)}\) one means equal odds; inf if the word fills the whole target corpus, 0 - the whole reference

A zero frequency in one of the corpora is replaced with 0.5 for %DIFF, Log Ratio and the odds ratio (Hardie 2014). The p-value of \(G^2\) comes from the chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom (calc_p_value). The module anyts.corpus.keyness gives them as the functions calc_log_likelihood, calc_chi2, calc_diff, calc_log_ratio, calc_bic, calc_ell and calc_odds_ratio of (a, b, c, d); their names and descriptions are in anyts.constants.KEYNESS_MEASURES.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description target list[str]/dict[str, int] - Words of the target corpus or their frequencies reference list[str]/dict[str, float]/FrequencyReference - Words of the reference corpus, their frequencies or a reference by frequencies measure str log_likelihood Measure of anyts.constants.KEYNESS_MEASURES for score and the sorting min_freq int 1 Minimum frequency of a keyword in its own corpus positive bool True Positive keywords (more frequent in the target corpus) or negative ones (more frequent in the reference) top_n int None Number of keywords; None - all of them

The parameters and the target corpus are checked by check_keyness_params. A reference that is not a list of strings, a counter or a FrequencyReference raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite frequency of a counter and an empty corpus raise SourceError.

check_keyness_params(measure="log_likelihood", min_freq=1, top_n=None, target=None) checks the parameters of keyness before a frequency dictionary is read: it raises ParameterError unless the measure is one of KEYNESS_MEASURES, the minimum frequency is an integer and the number of keywords is None or an integer of at least one. With target it also raises SourceTypeError unless the target corpus is a list of strings or a mapping of strings to whole frequencies, and SourceError for a negative, nan or infinite frequency.

docs.title: Reference by frequencies
docs.text:
FrequencyReference(counts, size, missing=0.0, key=None, keep=None) describes a reference corpus by its frequencies alone, such as a frequency dictionary built from a corpus too large to pass as words:

Field Type Default Description counts dict[str, float] - Frequencies of the keys in the reference corpus size float - Size of the reference corpus in words missing float 0.0 Frequency of a key missing from counts key callable None Key of a word of the target corpus in counts, such as its lemma; None - the word itself keep callable None Whether a word of the target corpus is counted; None - every word

Only the words of the target that keep passes are counted, under their key, in the frequencies and in the size alike. A key missing from counts has the frequency missing, such as the least frequency of a dictionary: an upper bound, so its word may be a positive keyword but never a negative one. Negative keywords come only from the keys of counts that keep passes. A frequency is checked as it is read, so a large dictionary is not gone through for positive keywords: one that is not a number raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite one SourceError. A size or a missing that is not a finite number or is negative raises ParameterError, and a key or a keep that cannot be called SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
A list of Keyword named tuples by descending keyness (ties broken by descending frequency and alphabetically, words of an undefined measure last); pd.DataFrame(keywords) gives a table.

Field Type Description word str Word freq_target int Frequency in the target corpus freq_reference float Frequency in the reference corpus ipm_target float Frequency in the target corpus per million words ipm_reference float Frequency in the reference corpus per million words g2 float Signed \(G^2\) p_value float p-value of \(G^2\) log_ratio float Log Ratio score float Value of the chosen measure

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Example

from anyts import WordsExtractor
from anyts.corpus import FrequencyReference, keyness

we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
target = we.extract(
    "The cat was at the window and watched the birds. The birds flew away and the cat "
    "fell asleep at the window. Tomorrow the cat will be at the window and watch the birds."
)
reference = we.extract(
    "The dog was on the floor and slept. Then the dog ate and slept again. "
    "Tomorrow the dog will go for a walk."
)

[(k.word, k.freq_target, round(k.g2, 2)) for k in keyness(target, reference, top_n=3)]
# [('at', 3, 3.1), ('birds', 3, 3.1), ('cat', 3, 3.1)]

[(k.word, round(k.g2, 2)) for k in keyness(target, reference, positive=False, top_n=2)]
# [('dog', -5.45), ('slept', -3.63)]

# Frequencies of the lemmas in a dictionary of a million words
counts = {
    "the": 60_000.0,
    "and": 28_000.0,
    "at": 5_000.0,
    "be": 6_000.0,
    "was": 9_000.0,
    "will": 3_000.0,
    "cat": 50.0,
    "window": 60.0,
    "bird": 40.0,
    "watch": 90.0,
    "away": 400.0,
    "tomorrow": 100.0,
}
lemmas = {"birds": "bird", "watched": "watch"}
dictionary = FrequencyReference(
    counts, size=1_000_000, missing=0.1, key=lambda word: lemmas.get(word, word)
)
[(k.word, round(k.g2, 1)) for k in keyness(target, dictionary, top_n=3)]
# [('bird', 40.0), ('cat', 38.7), ('window', 37.6)]

docs.title: KWIC concordance
docs.text: anyts.corpus.kwic(), anyts.corpus.format_kwic(), anyts.corpus.print_kwic(), anyts.corpus.Concordance

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
A KWIC concordance (keyword in context) - every occurrence of a word or a phrase with its context on both sides. Occurrences are found among the words of the text by the word form, ignoring case or respecting it (ignore_case=False), or by the lemma (by_lemma=True); the keyword is lemmatized as a string, so with a lemmatizer a phrase may be written in any form and without one it is given by lemmas. The words of a string and of the keyword come from the tokenizer, those of a Doc from its tokens: a tokenizer that splits a string as the pipeline does finds the same in both. Punctuation and symbols are not words; forms are compared in the composed form of Unicode (NFC), without soft hyphens.

A phrase does not cross the end of a paragraph or a sentence unless the keyword has a final mark or a sentence start in the same place (U.S. Army). A sentence ends at a boundary of a Doc anywhere between the words, an opening mark included, or, without boundaries or with partial ones (has_sents), at a sentence start of the sentence splitter, by default a final mark before whitespace. The context is window words on each side as written, punctuation included; whitespace collapses into one space, and occurrences do not overlap.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text:
The language enters through five parameters:

Parameter Default Description tokenize a run of word characters The words of a string and of the keyword as triples of the start, the end and the text lemmatize the word and the lemma of the model The lemmas of a word, given its text and its tokens in a Doc (none for a string and the keyword), or one lemma as a string; a word matches when one of its lemmas is one of those of the keyword fold str.lower The folding of a word form (with ignore_case) or a lemma before the comparison, such as the letters a language takes for the same join_hyphens False Join the parts of the hyphenated words of a Doc the tokenizer split (iter_doc_units); the default tokenizer then keeps them whole in a string and in the keyword too sentenize a final mark before whitespace The sentences of a string, of the keyword and of the text of a Doc without boundaries or with partial ones (has_sents) as triples of the start, the end and the text

A tokenize that does not give the words in order as triples of integer bounds within the string and a string raises SourceTypeError, and so does a sentenize whose triples do not lie within it; the sentences may come in any order. The words of a Doc are its tokens without a byte order mark at the start. By default the lemmas of a word are the word itself and, for a one-token word of a Doc with lemmas, the lemma of the model: a word is found by its own form, and a Doc of a pipeline with a lemmatizer by its lemmas.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str/Doc - Text or Doc object keyword str - Word or phrase window int 5 Number of words of context on each side by_lemma bool False Compare lemmas instead of word forms ignore_case bool True Ignore case when comparing word forms

A keyword without words and a negative window raise ParameterError; a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, a keyword that is not a string and a hook that is not callable raise SourceTypeError.

format_kwic(concordances, width=40) aligns the lines on the keyword: the left context is cut on the left and aligned to the right, the right one cut on the right; width is the width of a context in characters. The lines may come from any iterable and are taken in the composed form of Unicode (NFC), so the widths count characters as shown. Lines that are a string or cannot be iterated raise SourceTypeError, and a width that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

print_kwic(concordances, width=40) prints the result of format_kwic.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
A list of Concordance named tuples in the order of the text.

Field Type Description start int Position of the first character of the occurrence in the text end int Position after the last character of the occurrence left str Context on the left keyword str Occurrence as written in the text right str Context on the right

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Example

from anyts.corpus import kwic, print_kwic

text = (
    "The cat was at the window and watched the birds. The birds flew away and the cat "
    "fell asleep at the window. Tomorrow the cat will be at the window and watch the birds."
)
lines = kwic(text, "window", window=3)
lines[0]
# Concordance(start=19, end=25, left='was at the', keyword='window', right='and watched the')

print_kwic(lines, width=20)
#           was at the  window  and watched the
#        asleep at the  window  . Tomorrow the cat
#            be at the  window  and watch the

lemmas = {"watched": "watch", "birds": "bird"}
[
    line.keyword
    for line in kwic(
        text,
        "watch the bird",
        by_lemma=True,
        lemmatize=lambda word, tokens: [lemmas.get(word, word)],
    )
]
# ['watched the birds', 'watch the birds']

docs.title: Stylometry
docs.text: anyts.corpus.delta(), anyts.corpus.delta_profiles(), anyts.corpus.frequency_table(), anyts.corpus.z_scores(), anyts.corpus.zeta(), anyts.corpus.kilgarriff_chi2(), anyts.corpus.mendenhall_curve(), anyts.corpus.mendenhall_distance()

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Measures of stylometry and authorship attribution: distances between texts by the frequencies of the most frequent words (Burrows's Delta and its variants, as in stylo), markers of preferred and avoided words (Zeta), Kilgarriff's chi-square distance between corpora and the Mendenhall curve. The functions work on lists of units of a text: lower-case word forms (the usual choice for Delta), lemmas or character N-grams - case and lemmatization belong to the extractors.

docs.title: Burrows's Delta
docs.text:
A corpus is a dictionary "name of a text → units". frequency_table(corpus, n_mfw=100, culling=0.0) builds the table of relative frequencies: rows are the texts, columns the n_mfw most frequent units by descending mean relative frequency (alphabetically when equal); culling keeps the units that occur in at least the given share of the texts, as in stylo. A corpus that is not a mapping of lists of strings raises SourceTypeError; an empty corpus, a text without units and no unit left after culling raise SourceError, and an n_mfw that is not an integer of at least one and a culling that is not a number within [0, 1] ParameterError.

z_scores(table) standardizes the columns with the sample standard deviation, like scale() of R; a column with the same frequency in every text gives zeros.

delta computes a symmetric matrix of distances from the z-scores (a DataFrame with the names of the texts); at least three texts are needed - with two, the z-scores degenerate to ±1/√2 and the distances do not depend on the frequencies.

Variants (anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS), with the formulas of the sources of stylo; \(n\) is the number of units, \(z_A\) and \(z_B\) the vectors of z-scores of the texts:

Variant Key Formula Source Burrows's Delta burrows \(\frac{1}{n} \sum_i \lvert z_{A,i} - z_{B,i} \rvert\) Burrows (2002), dist.delta Quadratic Delta quadratic \(\frac{1}{n} \sqrt{\sum_i (z_{A,i} - z_{B,i})^2}\) Argamon (2008), dist.argamon Eder's Delta eder \(\sum_i \frac{n - i + 2}{n} \lvert z_{A,i} - z_{B,i} \rvert\), \(i\) - rank of the unit by frequency Eder, dist.eder Cosine Delta cosine \(1 - \frac{z_A \cdot z_B}{\lVert z_A \rVert \lVert z_B \rVert}\) Smith and Aldridge (2011), Evert et al. (2015), dist.wurzburg

Cosine Delta clusters the texts by author best in the experiments of Evert et al. The usual number of units is 100 to 500 most frequent words, 100-200 for character N-grams.

Parameters of delta:

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them variant str burrows Variant of Delta of anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in

The corpus, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table; fewer than three texts raise SourceError, and an unknown variant ParameterError.

delta_profiles(reference, samples, n_mfw, variant, culling, statistics) is for authorship attribution. The most frequent units, the culling and the statistics of the z-scores come from the reference texts (the profiles of the authors) or from a separate set statistics, such as training windows when the profiles are too few to estimate the spread of the frequencies; the texts under test samples get the same units and scaling. The result is the distances from the samples (rows) to the references (columns); the nearest reference is the presumed author. Unlike in delta, a sample affects neither the units nor the scaling, so its result does not depend on the other samples. The corpora, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table; fewer than three texts for the statistics raise SourceError, and an unknown variant ParameterError.

Example

from anyts import WordsExtractor
from anyts.corpus import delta, delta_profiles, frequency_table

texts = {
    "A": (
        "The cat was at the window and watched the birds. "
        "The birds flew away and the cat slept at the window."
    ),
    "B": "The dog was on the floor and slept. Then the dog ate and slept again on the floor.",
    "C": "Tomorrow the cat will come back to the window and watch the birds, but the dog will sleep.",
}
we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
corpus = {name: we.extract(text) for name, text in texts.items()}

frequency_table(corpus, n_mfw=5).round(3)
#      the    and    dog  slept  birds
# A  0.286  0.095  0.000  0.048  0.095
# B  0.222  0.111  0.111  0.111  0.000
# C  0.222  0.056  0.056  0.000  0.056

delta(corpus, n_mfw=5).round(3)
#        A      B      C
# A  0.000  1.483  1.161
# B  1.483  0.000  1.219
# C  1.161  1.219  0.000

delta(corpus, n_mfw=5, variant="cosine").round(3)
#        A      B      C
# A  0.000  1.676  1.273
# B  1.676  0.000  1.525
# C  1.273  1.525  0.000

sample = {"?": we.extract("The cat woke up at the window and watched the birds again.")}
delta_profiles(corpus, sample, n_mfw=5).round(3)
#        A      B      C
# ?  0.499  1.493  0.662

docs.title: Zeta
docs.text:
Markers of preferred and avoided words after Burrows (2007) and Craig and Kinney (2009). Every text of both corpora is split into segments of about segment_size words (the length over the size rounded half up, at least one segment); \(DP\) is the share of the segments of a corpus with the word. Zeta is \(DP_{target} - DP_{comparison}\), from −1 to 1 (zeta.craig in stylo; the classic Zeta of Craig, \(DP_{target} + (1 - DP_{comparison})\), is greater by one); the logarithmic Zeta is \(\log_2 \frac{DP_{target}}{DP_{comparison}}\) (Schöch et al. 2018), a zero share replaced by half a segment. The list goes from the words the target corpus prefers to those it avoids.

Parameter Type Default Description target list[str]/list[list[str]] - Words of the target corpus - one text or a list of texts comparison list[str]/list[list[str]] - Words of the comparison corpus segment_size int 2000 Size of a segment in words top_n int None Number of words from the start of the list; None - all of them

The result is a list of ZetaScore(word, dp_target, dp_comparison, zeta, log_zeta) named tuples by descending Zeta, by descending logarithmic Zeta and alphabetically when equal. A corpus that is neither a list of strings nor a list of such lists raises SourceTypeError, and a corpus without words SourceError; a segment_size or a top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

Example

from anyts.corpus import zeta

zeta(corpus["A"], corpus["B"], segment_size=5, top_n=2)
# [ZetaScore(word='at', dp_target=0.5, dp_comparison=0.0, zeta=0.5, log_zeta=2.0),
#  ZetaScore(word='birds', dp_target=0.5, dp_comparison=0.0, zeta=0.5, log_zeta=2.0)]

zeta(corpus["A"], corpus["B"], segment_size=5)[-1]
# ZetaScore(word='on', dp_target=0.0, dp_comparison=0.5, zeta=-0.5, log_zeta=-2.0)

docs.title: Kilgarriff's chi-square
docs.text:
The distance between two corpora after Kilgarriff (2001): for the n_mfw most frequent words of the joint corpus the expected frequencies in the corpora are proportional to their sizes, \(\chi^2 = \sum (O - E)^2 / E\) over the words and both corpora. The greater the value, the more the corpora differ; it grows with the size of the corpora, so only pairs of equal sizes are comparable.

Parameter Type Default Description words_a list[str] - Words of the first corpus words_b list[str] - Words of the second corpus n_mfw int 500 Number of the most frequent words of the joint corpus

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, a corpus without words SourceError, and an n_mfw that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

Example

from anyts.corpus import kilgarriff_chi2

round(kilgarriff_chi2(corpus["A"], corpus["B"], n_mfw=5), 3)
# 4.113

docs.title: Mendenhall curve
docs.text:
mendenhall_curve(words) - the shares of the words of every length in characters (Mendenhall 1887), a profile of the author comparable between texts whatever their size. Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and no words SourceError.

mendenhall_distance(words_a, words_b) - the Jensen-Shannon distance with base 2 between the curves, from 0 (the distributions coincide) to 1. Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and a text without words SourceError.

Example

from anyts.corpus import mendenhall_curve, mendenhall_distance

{length: round(share, 3) for length, share in mendenhall_curve(corpus["A"]).items()}
# {2: 0.095, 3: 0.524, 4: 0.095, 5: 0.143, 6: 0.095, 7: 0.048}

round(mendenhall_distance(corpus["A"], corpus["B"]), 3)
# 0.303

docs.title: Character N-gram extraction
docs.text: anyts.extractors.CharNgramsExtractor

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
A class for extracting character N-grams from a text - sequences of N characters taken with a sliding window over the string. Character N-grams are a standard feature of stylometry and authorship attribution (Stamatatos 2009) and can replace words in measures such as Burrows's Delta.

Whitespace runs are collapsed into a single space, punctuation marks are kept. With within_words=True N-grams do not cross word boundaries: the text is split into words by the tokenizer, punctuation is dropped, and words shorter than N yield no N-grams.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text: The default word tokenizer for within_words is the method tokenize(text), which a language library overrides in a subclass. Here it is the default tokenizer of WordsExtractor: a word character \w followed by word characters, combining marks, zero-width joiners and non-joiners and soft hyphens, so don't gives the words don and t. The messages of its errors come from the class attribute messages, MESSAGES by default.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description n int 2 N-gram length in characters lowercase bool False Convert the text to lower case within_words bool False Take N-grams only inside words tokenizer Pattern/Callable None Word tokenizer for within_words or a regular expression; by default the tokenize method

An n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: extract
docs.text:
Extracts N-grams from a text.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string

A text that is not a string raises SourceTypeError, and so does, with within_words, a tokenizer that cannot be called or does not return strings.

Example

Code:

from anyts import CharNgramsExtractor

text = "The cat slept  on the sill, and the dog - on the floor."

CharNgramsExtractor(n=3, lowercase=True).extract(text)[:6]

Result:

('the', 'he ', 'e c', ' ca', 'cat', 'at ')

N-grams inside words only:

Example

Code:

CharNgramsExtractor(n=4, lowercase=True, within_words=True).extract(text)

Result:

('slep', 'lept', 'sill', 'floo', 'loor')

docs.title: get_most_common
docs.text:
Returns the top N-grams of the text as a list of (N-gram, frequency) pairs, the most frequent first; a number that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description n int 10 Number of top N-grams

Warning

The method must be called after N-grams have been extracted with extract.

Example

Code:

ce = CharNgramsExtractor(n=3, lowercase=True)
ce.extract(text)
ce.get_most_common(2)

Result:

[('the', 4), ('he ', 4)]

docs.title: Sentence extraction
docs.text: anyts.extractors.SentsExtractor, anyts.extractors.iter_part_sents(), anyts.extractors.FixedSentsExtractor

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A class for extracting sentences from a text. It allows using different tokenizers and setting the minimum and maximum length of extracted sentences.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text:
The default tokenizer is the method sentenize(text), which a language library overrides in a subclass. Here it splits the text at whitespace after ., !, ? or …, optionally followed by a closing quote or bracket; it knows no abbreviations, so e.g. this is two sentences. A piece without words, such as the dots of a spaced ellipsis . . . or a lone !, stays with the sentence before it, or with the one after it at the start of the text. The messages of its errors come from the class attribute messages, MESSAGES by default.

Note

A spaCy pipeline can be passed as the tokenizer: tokenizer=lambda text: (sent.text for sent in nlp(text).sents).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description tokenizer Pattern/Callable None Tokenizer or regular expression; by default the sentenize method min_len int 0 Minimum length of an extracted sentence in characters, 0 for no bound max_len int 0 Maximum length of an extracted sentence in characters, 0 for no bound

Note

A regular expression as the tokenizer is a separator for re.split. A blank line - a line break, optional whitespace and another line break - ends a sentence of any tokenizer: the text is split at blank lines first and every part goes to the tokenizer, so a heading or a paragraph without a final mark is a sentence of its own, and so is a part without words, such as a line of asterisks, which the statistics leave out. The sentences are stripped of whitespace at the edges before the length bounds, and empty ones are dropped.

A length bound that is not an integer, a negative bound and a minimum above the maximum raise ParameterError.

docs.title: extract
docs.text:
Extracts sentences from a text.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string

A text that is not a string and a tokenizer that cannot be called or does not return strings raise SourceTypeError.

An example of sentence extraction with the default tokenizer:

Example

Code:

from anyts import SentsExtractor

SentsExtractor().extract('It rains. Does it? He said "Yes!" Then he left.')

Result:

('It rains.', 'Does it?', 'He said "Yes!"', 'Then he left.')

An example of sentence extraction from paragraphs without a final mark:

Example

Code:

from anyts import SentsExtractor

SentsExtractor().extract("What is new\n\nFaster import\nFewer bugs\n\nThanks for reading!")

Result:

('What is new', 'Faster import\nFewer bugs', 'Thanks for reading!')

An example of sentence extraction with a regular expression as the tokenizer:

Example

Code:

import re

from anyts import SentsExtractor

SentsExtractor(tokenizer=re.compile(r", ")).extract("Rain today, sun tomorrow")

Result:

('Rain today', 'sun tomorrow')

docs.title: Sentences of the parts of a text
docs.text: iter_part_sents(iter_sents, text) runs a splitter - iter_sents, giving the start, the end and the text of every sentence of a string - on every part of a text between blank lines (BLANK_LINE) and gives the sentences at their positions in the whole text, so that a blank line ends a sentence whatever the splitter, as in SentsExtractor. A text that is not a string raises SourceTypeError, and so does an iter_sents that cannot be called or does not give the sentences of a part in order, as triples of integer bounds within it and a string.

docs.title: Ready sentences
docs.text: FixedSentsExtractor(sents) of anyts.extractors gives the sentences it was made with for any text, so a class that takes a sentence extractor gets known sentences without splitting the text again. Sentences that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Word extraction
docs.text: anyts.extractors.WordsExtractor, anyts.extractors.FixedWordsExtractor

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A class for extracting words from a text. It allows using different tokenizers, filtering stop words, numbers and punctuation, lemmatizing, building N-grams, and setting the minimum and maximum length of extracted words.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text:
A language library overrides these hooks in a subclass:

Hook Kind Default Used for tokenize(text) method a word character \w followed by word characters, combining marks, zero-width joiners and non-joiners and soft hyphens, so that a word in NFD, in Devanagari or in Persian with U+200C stays whole the tokenizer when tokenizer is not given lemmatize(word) method the word itself use_lexemes=True number_pattern class attribute a signed number with separators and an optional percent sign: -5, 1990-1995, 1,500.50, 12/03/2020, 3:30, 10% filter_nums=True, matched against the whole lower-cased word messages class attribute MESSAGES the errors of the parameters, of the text and of the tokenizer

Example

import re

from anyts import WordsExtractor


class EnglishWords(WordsExtractor):
    number_pattern = re.compile(r"\d+(?:st|nd|rd|th)?")

    def tokenize(self, text):
        return text.split()


EnglishWords(filter_nums=True).extract("The 3rd time")

Result:

('The', 'time')

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description tokenizer Pattern/Callable None Tokenizer or regular expression; by default the tokenize method filter_punct bool True Filter punctuation marks filter_nums bool False Filter numbers matched by number_pattern use_lexemes bool False Use word lemmas of the lemmatize method stopwords Collection[str] None Stop words, compared case-insensitively lowercase bool False Convert words to lower case ngram_range Tuple[int, int] (1, 1) Lower and upper bound of the N-gram size min_len int 0 Minimum length of an extracted word in characters, 0 for no bound max_len int 0 Maximum length of an extracted word in characters, 0 for no bound

Note

A regular expression as the tokenizer is a separator for re.split. The filters are applied in order: punctuation, numbers, lemmatization, lower case, stop words, word length. A punctuation mark is a token of marks and symbols only, multi-character ones included: ?!, --, …, € (anyts.utils.is_punctuation). Empty and whitespace tokens are dropped before the filters. N-grams join the words with _.

An ngram_range that is not a pair of integers, or whose lower bound is below one or above the upper one, raises ParameterError, and so do a length bound that is not an integer, a negative bound and a minimum above the maximum. Stop words that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: extract
docs.text:
Extracts words from a text.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string

A text that is not a string and a tokenizer that cannot be called or does not return strings raise SourceTypeError.

An example of word extraction with bigrams as tokens, after filtering numbers and stop words:

Example

Code:

from anyts import WordsExtractor

text = "Better 100 friends than 100 dollars"

we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True, stopwords=["than"], filter_nums=True, ngram_range=(1, 2))
we.extract(text)

Result:

('better', 'friends', 'dollars', 'better_friends', 'friends_dollars')

docs.title: get_most_common
docs.text:
Returns the top words of the text as a list of (word, frequency) pairs, the most frequent first; a number that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description n int 10 Number of top words

Warning

The method must be called after words have been extracted with extract.

Example

Code:

from anyts import WordsExtractor

we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
we.extract("The cat saw the dog and the bird")
we.get_most_common(2)

Result:

[('the', 3), ('cat', 1)]

docs.title: Ready words
docs.text: FixedWordsExtractor(words) of anyts.extractors gives the words it was made with for any text, so a class that takes a word extractor gets known words without tokenizing the text again. Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Basic statistics
docs.text: anyts.basic_stats.BasicStats, anyts.basic_stats.count_punctuations(), anyts.basic_stats.dash_pattern()

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The basic statistics of a text: the counts of its sentences, words, characters, letters, spaces, syllables and punctuation marks, the distributions of the words by letters and by syllables, and the long, complex, simple, monosyllabic and polysyllabic words. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy. Letters are counted by str.isalpha, so digits, hyphens and marks inside a word are not letters.

The words and the sentences of a string come from the extractors. A Doc gives its tokens as words, without punctuation marks and symbols such as € or %, and its boundaries as sentences, or those of the sentence extractor when it has none or only partial ones (has_sents); an extractor given is used on its text instead. A blank line ends a sentence of a string and of a Doc without boundaries; a Doc with boundaries does so when its pipeline has start_sents_after_blank_lines (registered by a language library under its own name) before the parser, senter or sentencizer. A sentence without words, such as punctuation alone, is not counted.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text:
A language library subclasses BasicStats:

Hook Kind Description count_syllables(word) method The syllables of a word; abstract sents_extractor_class, words_extractor_class class attributes The extractors used when none is given; SentsExtractor and WordsExtractor by default join_hyphens class attribute Join the parts of the hyphenated words of a Doc (iter_doc_words); False by default count_punctuations(text) method The punctuation marks by type; count_punctuations of the module by default stats_desc class attribute The counts of get_stats with their descriptions for print_stats; anyts.constants.BASIC_STATS_DESC by default

The other hooks, stats_headers, level_scales and messages, come from Stats. The thresholds of the complex and the long words are parameters; a library sets its own defaults in its __init__ and passes them on.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
