Parameter Type Default Description source str/Doc - Data source (a string or a Doc object) sents_extractor SentsExtractor None Sentence extraction tool; used for a Doc too, on its text words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool; used for a Doc too, on its text normalize bool False Compute normalized statistics complex_syl_factor int COMPLEX_SYL_FACTOR Minimum number of syllables in a complex word long_word_letter_factor int LONG_WORD_LETTER_FACTOR Minimum number of letters in a long word

A source that is neither a string nor a Doc and an extractor of another type raise SourceTypeError, a source without words SourceError, a threshold that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

The thresholds of the core are COMPLEX_SYL_FACTOR = 3 and LONG_WORD_LETTER_FACTOR = 7 of anyts.constants.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description normalize bool Whether the normalized statistics are computed complex_syl_factor int Minimum number of syllables in a complex word long_word_letter_factor int Minimum number of letters in a long word c_letters dict[int, int] Distribution of words by number of letters c_syllables dict[int, int] Distribution of words by number of syllables n_sents int Number of sentences containing words n_words int Number of words n_unique_words int Number of unique words, case ignored n_long_words int Number of long words n_complex_words int Number of complex words n_simple_words int Number of simple words: with a syllable, below the complex ones n_monosyllable_words int Number of monosyllabic words n_polysyllable_words int Number of polysyllabic words n_chars int Number of characters without the line breaks n_letters int Number of letters n_spaces int Number of spaces of Unicode (category Zs), such as the no-break space, and tabs n_syllables int Number of syllables n_punctuations int Number of punctuation marks c_punctuations dict[str, int] Distribution of punctuation marks by type p_unique_words float Normalized number of unique words p_long_words float Normalized number of long words p_complex_words float Normalized number of complex words p_simple_words float Normalized number of simple words p_monosyllable_words float Normalized number of monosyllabic words p_polysyllable_words float Normalized number of polysyllabic words p_letters float Normalized number of letters p_spaces float Normalized number of spaces p_punctuations float Normalized number of punctuation marks

With normalize=True the counts of the words are divided by the number of words, those of the characters by the number of characters.

docs.title: count_words_by_syllables, count_words_by_letters
docs.text: count_words_by_syllables(min_syllables) and count_words_by_letters(min_letters) return the number of words with at least the given number of syllables or letters; a minimum that is not an integer raises ParameterError.

docs.title: get_stats
docs.text: Returns a dictionary with the distributions c_letters and c_syllables, the counts of stats_desc, the distribution c_punctuations and, with normalize=True, the normalized counts, as a copy: editing it does not change the object. With flat=True the distributions give a key for every value the text has, such as c_letters_3 and c_punctuations_comma.

docs.title: print_stats
docs.text:
Prints a table with the counts of stats_desc, their descriptions and the headers from stats_headers.

The frame of the statistics (to_dataframe) and their reading (describe) are those of the statistics interface.

docs.title: Punctuation marks
docs.text:
count_punctuations(text, marks, dash_pattern) counts punctuation marks by type, the distribution of c_punctuations: commas, periods, question and exclamation marks, ellipses, colons, semicolons, dashes, hyphens, guillemets, quotation marks, parentheses and other marks. Dashes typed with hyphens (dash_pattern) are counted first, then ellipses - …, three or more periods, or two after ? and !, one mark whose periods are not counted as periods (Who?.. is a question and an ellipsis) - then each mark by its type in marks; any other character of the Unicode categories P and S is another mark (§, €, °). A mark of marks that is not a single character or has an unknown type raises ParameterError; a text that is not a string, marks that are not a mapping and a dash_pattern that is not a compiled regular expression raise SourceTypeError.

In the core the types are anyts.constants.PUNCTUATION_TYPES, and marks and dash_pattern are PUNCTUATION_MARKS and DASH_PATTERN of anyts.basic_stats. The marks count ¿ and ¡ as question and exclamation marks (¿So? has two), —, – and the horizontal bar ― as dashes, «» as guillemets and "“”‘’ as quotation marks; a hyphen inside a word, before a digit or at a line break inside a word is a hyphen (well-known, -5). A dash typed with hyphens is a run of two or more hyphens, or a hyphen after whitespace, a closing mark or at the start of a line, before a space of a line (a Unicode separator such as the no-break space, or a tab: SPACES) or the end of the text, or between a letter and an opening or a closing mark (--Hello --said John, - They left - he said).

docs.title: Dashes typed with hyphens
docs.text:
dash_pattern(conjunctions, hanging_before_comma) builds the dash_pattern of count_punctuations. A hanging hyphen glued to a letter or a digit and carried on to a later word (pre- and post-war, 5- and 10-year) stays a hyphen before spaces of a line and one of the conjunctions, case ignored, and with hanging_before_comma before a comma (two-, three- and four-year). A language whose dialogue closes a line with a hyphen before a comma (-Come -he said-, and left) leaves hanging_before_comma off. Without the parameters the pattern is DASH_PATTERN. Conjunctions that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, and an empty conjunction ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description conjunctions Collection[str] () Conjunctions after a hanging hyphen hanging_before_comma bool False Take a hyphen between a letter and a comma for a hanging one

Example

from anyts.basic_stats import count_punctuations, dash_pattern

text = "pre- and post-war, two-, three- and four-year - he said"
counts = count_punctuations(text, dash_pattern=dash_pattern(["and"], hanging_before_comma=True))
counts["dash"], counts["hyphen"]
# (1, 5)

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
A subclass with the syllables of a language - here the groups of vowels, a rough rule for English.

Example

import re

from anyts.basic_stats import BasicStats


class Stats(BasicStats):
    def count_syllables(self, word):
        return len(re.findall(r"[aeiouy]+", word, re.IGNORECASE))


bs = Stats("The cat sat on the mat. A beautiful day!")
bs.n_sents, bs.n_words, bs.n_syllables, bs.n_complex_words
# (2, 9, 11, 1)
bs.c_punctuations["exclamation"]
# 1

docs.title: Cohesion statistics
docs.text: anyts.cohesion_stats.CohesionStats

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The cohesion statistics of a text in the manner of Coh-Metrix: the overlap of the nouns, the arguments (nouns and pronouns) and the content words between adjacent and between all pairs of sentences, the givenness (pronouns, demonstratives, lemmas used before), the temporal cohesion (the repetition of the tense and the aspect of the verbs of adjacent sentences) and the connectors of a dictionary by class and kind per 1000 words. The sentences are compared by lemmas. The data source is a Doc object of spaCy with the parts of speech and the lemmas, split into sentences by its boundaries, or by the sentence extractor over its text when one is given or the Doc has none.

An extractor of another type, a source that is not a Doc and connectors that are not a dictionary of phrases and pairs of strings raise SourceTypeError; a source without parts of speech, lemmas or words raises SourceError, and an unknown class or kind of a connector ParameterError.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text:
A language library subclasses CohesionStats. By default the words and their features are read from a Doc by Universal Dependencies, and there are no connectors:

Hook Kind Description analyze(source) method Words of the sentences of a source as CohesionWord: the word, its lemma, its part of speech, whether it is a noun, a pronoun, a demonstrative, an argument and a content word, its tense, mood and aspect; by default those of a Doc, sentence by sentence (doc_units), with the features of word_info; a library that reads a string or a Doc without these annotations overrides it doc_units(doc) method Words of the sentences of a Doc as lists of tokens: by its boundaries, or by the extractor over its text (split_doc_units of anyts.utils) word_info(unit) method Features of a word of a Doc; by default a noun is NOUN or PROPN, a pronoun PRON or a possessive, demonstrative or personal determiner, a demonstrative carries PronType=Dem, an argument is NOUN, PROPN or PRON, a content word one of anyts.constants.CONTENT_UD_POS and no demonstrative, and the tense, the mood and the aspect are the features Tense, Mood and Aspect load_connectors() class method Dictionary of the connectors of the language, class and kind by connector; empty by default connector_matcher() class method Matcher of that dictionary, built once for a class and shared by its instances and by searches outside the statistics connector_matcher_class class attribute Class that finds the connectors with the context rules of the language; ConnectorMatcher by default. A matcher with other classes or kinds gives other connectors_* attributes, so the subclass sets its own stats_desc too temporal_features class attribute Features of the verbs whose repetitions make the temporal cohesion: a tuple of one or more distinct ones of tense, mood and aspect (TEMPORAL_FEATURES), checked when the class is defined; tense and aspect by default, as in Coh-Metrix sents_extractor_class, join_hyphens class attributes Sentence extractor of a Doc without boundaries, joining of the hyphenated words of a Doc stats_desc, stats_headers class attributes Statistics of get_stats with their descriptions (COHESION_STATS_DESC by default), headers of the columns for print_stats messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

The parameters of a library - its model of a string, its word extractor - go to the constructor of its subclass, which keeps them for its analyze. An analyze that does not give sentences of CohesionWord objects raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description source Doc - Data source: a Doc with the parts of speech and the lemmas, or what analyze reads sents_extractor SentsExtractor None Sentence extraction tool; given here, it splits a Doc by its text whatever its boundaries connectors dict[str, tuple[str, str]] None Class and kind by connector; those of load_connectors by default

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description words, lemmas tuple[tuple[str]] Words and lemmas of every sentence with words n_sents, n_words int Numbers of the sentences with words and of the words n_nouns, n_pronouns, n_demonstratives, n_content_words int Numbers of the words by kind n_given int Number of the content words whose lemma was used before n_connectors, connector_spans, c_connectors int, tuple[Connector], dict[str, int] Number of the connectors, their occurrences and their number by connector noun_overlap_adjacent, noun_overlap_all float Shares of the adjacent and of all pairs of sentences sharing a noun argument_overlap_adjacent, argument_overlap_all float The same for a noun or a pronoun content_overlap_adjacent, content_overlap_all float The same for a content word content_overlap_prop_adjacent, content_overlap_prop_all float Mean share of the shared content words (Dice) in the adjacent and in all pairs p_pronouns, p_demonstratives float Shares of the pronouns and of the demonstratives among the words pronoun_noun_ratio float Ratio of the pronouns to the nouns p_given float Share of the content words whose lemma was used before in the text tense_repetition, mood_repetition, aspect_repetition float Shares of the adjacent pairs of sentences with the same dominant tense, mood and aspect temporal_cohesion float Mean of the repetitions of temporal_features connectors float Connectors per 1000 words connectors_<class>, connectors_<kind> float Connectors of every class and kind of the matcher per 1000 words: connectors_causal, connectors_adversative, connectors_concessive, connectors_temporal, connectors_additive, connectors_conditional, connectors_reformulative, connectors_primary and connectors_secondary by default

An overlap of a text of one sentence, a repetition without two adjacent sentences with the feature, and a share without anything to divide by are nan.

The methods get_stats, to_dataframe, print_stats and describe are those of the statistics interface.

docs.title: Metric functions
docs.text: The overlaps, the givenness, the repetitions and the search of the connectors are described in the metric functions section.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

import spacy
from spacy.tokens import Doc

from anyts.cohesion_stats import CohesionStats


class English(CohesionStats):
    @classmethod
    def load_connectors(cls):
        return {"however": ("adversative", "secondary")}


# The cat slept. However, the cat woke.
doc = Doc(
    spacy.blank("en").vocab,
    words=["The", "cat", "slept", ".", "However", ",", "the", "cat", "woke", "."],
    spaces=[True, True, False, True, False, True, True, True, False, False],
    pos=["DET", "NOUN", "VERB", "PUNCT", "ADV", "PUNCT", "DET", "NOUN", "VERB", "PUNCT"],
    lemmas=["the", "cat", "sleep", ".", "however", ",", "the", "cat", "wake", "."],
    morphs=["", "", "Aspect=Perf|Tense=Past", "", "", "", "", "", "Aspect=Perf|Tense=Past", ""],
    sent_starts=[True, False, False, False, True, False, False, False, False, False],
)
stats = English(doc)
stats.noun_overlap_adjacent, stats.temporal_cohesion
# (1.0, 1.0)
stats.connector_spans
# (Connector(sent=1, start=0, end=1, text='however', cls='adversative', kind='secondary'),)

docs.title: Metric functions
docs.text:
anyts.cohesion_stats

Functions that measure how the sentences of a text are tied together by shared elements, in the manner of Coh-Metrix, and the search of the connectors that tie them. A sentence is given as the collection of its elements (lemmas of nouns, arguments or content words, values of a feature of its verbs), which a library chooses, so the functions see no language.

A list of sentences that is a string, a Doc, an iterator, a set or a table raises SourceTypeError, and so does a sentence that is not a list of strings (check_words), such as a list of spaCy tokens. The overlaps (calc_overlap, calc_proportional_overlap, calc_overlaps) take a sentence as a set too; count_given and calc_repetition count the words in order and refuse a set.

docs.title: calc_overlap
docs.text:
The binary overlap of Coh-Metrix (CRFNO1, CRFAO1, CRFSO1 over the adjacent pairs, CRFNOa, CRFAOa, CRFSOa over all of them): the share of the pairs of sentences that share at least one element; nan for a text shorter than two sentences. All the pairs are counted as in calc_overlaps, without going through them.

Parameter Type Default Description sets list[set[str]] - Elements of every sentence adjacent bool True Count the adjacent pairs only, otherwise all the pairs

docs.title: calc_proportional_overlap
docs.text:
The proportional overlap of Coh-Metrix (CRFCWO1, CRFCWOa): the Dice coefficient of a pair of sentences averaged over the pairs; nan for a text shorter than two sentences. Over all the pairs the sum is computed as in calc_overlaps, without going through them.

Parameter Type Default Description sets list[set[str]] - Elements of every sentence adjacent bool True Count the adjacent pairs only, otherwise all the pairs

docs.title: dice
docs.text:
The Dice coefficient of two sets:

\[ \frac{2 \times |A \cap B|}{|A| + |B|} \]

and 0 for two empty sets.

Parameter Type Default Description first frozenset[str] - First set second frozenset[str] - Second set

docs.title: calc_overlaps
docs.text:
The values of calc_overlap and calc_proportional_overlap over the adjacent and over all the pairs at once, as an Overlap named tuple with the fields adjacent, all, prop_adjacent and prop_all; without proportional the last two are nan. The values over all the pairs are computed without going through every pair: the sharing pairs are counted over bit masks of the sentences, and the sum of the Dice coefficients over the histograms of the lengths of the sentences holding each element, added by math.fsum so that it does not depend on the order of the elements.

Parameter Type Default Description sets list[set[str]] - Elements of every sentence proportional bool True Compute the proportional overlap as well

docs.title: count_given
docs.text:
The number of given elements: an element is given when the same lemma was used earlier in any sentence, the current one included; the first occurrence is new.

Parameter Type Default Description sents list[list[str]] - Lemmas of every sentence in the order of the text

docs.title: dominant
docs.text:
The dominant value: the most frequent one, the first of the equally frequent; None for an empty list.

Parameter Type Default Description values list[str] - Values

docs.title: calc_repetition
docs.text:
The repetition of the tense and of the aspect of Coh-Metrix (SMTEMP): the share of the adjacent pairs of sentences whose verbs have the same dominant value of the feature; a pair where one of the sentences has no verb with the feature is skipped, and without a single such pair the value is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description sents list[list[str]] - Values of the feature of the verbs of every sentence

Example

from anyts.cohesion_stats import calc_overlaps, calc_repetition, count_given

calc_overlaps([{"cat", "house"}, {"cat", "dog"}, {"bird"}])
# Overlap(adjacent=0.5, all=0.3333333333333333, prop_adjacent=0.25, prop_all=0.16666666666666666)
count_given([["cat", "house"], ["cat", "dog"], ["house"]])
# 2
calc_repetition([["Pres"], ["Pres", "Past", "Pres"], ["Past"]])
# 0.5

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text:
ConnectorMatcher(connectors) finds the connectors (discourse markers: because, however, on the other hand) of a dictionary in the sentences of a text. The dictionary gives the class of every connector - causal, adversative, concessive, temporal, additive, conditional or reformulative (CONNECTOR_CLASSES) - and its kind, primary or secondary (CONNECTOR_KINDS). A connector is matched by the normalized forms of its words, the longest one at every position, without overlaps; a period or a hyphen inside a connector may be split off by the tokenizer (e.g. as e, g). An occurrence is a Connector: the number of the sentence sent, the positions start and end of its words, the connector text as the dictionary writes it, its class cls and kind kind.

A dictionary that is not a mapping of a phrase to a pair of strings raises SourceTypeError, an unknown class or kind ParameterError.

The rules of a language are class attributes of a subclass, empty by default apart from pos_tags:

Hook Kind Description normalize(text) method Normalized form of a word and of a connector; the lower case by default blocked_after, blocked_before class attributes Words after or before a connector, by its text, that make it no connector (before the end) blocked_after_pos class attribute Parts of speech of the word after a connector, by its text, that make it no connector not_at_start class attribute Connectors that do not count at the start of a sentence, where they open a reply (Well, ...) only_after class attribute Connectors that count inside a sentence only after these words pos_tags, pos_extra class attributes Parts of speech of a one-word connector, CONNECTOR_POS of Universal Dependencies by default, and those allowed for a word on top of them not_after_pos class attribute Parts of speech of the previous word that make a one-word connector no connector (a determiner: the before and the after) start_only_pos class attribute Parts of speech of a one-word connector that counts only at the start of a sentence (a capitalized connector tagged as a proper noun) classes, kinds class attributes Classes and kinds of the dictionary; CONNECTOR_CLASSES and CONNECTOR_KINDS by default messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

The words of the lists and the keys of pos_extra are normalized forms, while the other lists are keyed by the connector as the dictionary writes it. A rule that is not a collection of strings, or a mapping of strings to them, raises SourceTypeError when the class is defined.

docs.title: find
docs.text:
find(words, sent_index, pos) returns the occurrences of the connectors in a sentence in the order of its words. The words are those of one sentence without punctuation, the first one its start. With the parts of speech, a one-word connector counts only with one of pos_tags or of pos_extra for its form, never after one of not_after_pos, and with one of start_only_pos only at the start of the sentence; a word without a part of speech (None) passes. Without the parts of speech the rules that read them are skipped.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the sentence sent_index int 0 Number of the sentence, written into the occurrences pos list[str] None Parts of speech of the words

Words that are not a list of strings and parts of speech that are not a list of strings and None (the tags token.pos_ of spaCy, not the numbers token.pos) raise SourceTypeError, a number of the sentence that is not an integer and parts of speech not as many as the words ParameterError.

Example

from anyts.cohesion_stats import ConnectorMatcher


class Matcher(ConnectorMatcher):
    blocked_after = {"before": frozenset({"the"})}
    not_after_pos = frozenset({"DET"})


matcher = Matcher(
    {
        "however": ("adversative", "secondary"),
        "before": ("temporal", "primary"),
        "and": ("additive", "primary"),
        "on the other hand": ("adversative", "secondary"),
    }
)
matcher.find("On the other hand he left before the end".split())
# [Connector(sent=0, start=0, end=4, text='on the other hand', cls='adversative', kind='secondary')]
matcher.find(["The", "before", "and", "after"], pos=["DET", "ADV", "CCONJ", "ADV"])
# [Connector(sent=0, start=2, end=3, text='and', cls='additive', kind='primary')]

docs.title: Lexical diversity metrics
docs.text: anyts.diversity_stats.DiversityStats

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
A class for computing the main lexical diversity metrics of a text from its words.

Note

The metrics are computed by accessing an attribute or by calling get_stats.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text: The class takes the words as given: a language library extracts them from its sources (a string, a spaCy Doc) and lower-cases them, since every metric counts lexemes. A library overrides two class attributes in a subclass: stats_desc, the metrics of get_stats with their descriptions for print_stats (anyts.constants.DIVERSITY_STATS_DESC by default), and stats_headers, the two column headers of print_stats. Error messages come from the class attribute messages, MESSAGES by default.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description words Iterable[str] - Words of the text: a sequence or an iterator of strings window_len int 50 Window size for MATTR and segment size for MSTTR (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN) mtld_threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD) mtld_min_len int 10 Minimum factor length for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W (MTLD_MIN_LEN) hdd_sample_size int 42 Sample size for HD-D (HDD_SAMPLE_SIZE) log_base float 10 Logarithm base for the Summer, Maas and Dugast metrics (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

Words that are not a sequence or an iterator of strings raise SourceTypeError, and so do a string, a Doc, a set and a table; no words raise SourceError.

The parameters are checked by check_params(window_len, mtld_threshold, mtld_min_len, hdd_sample_size, log_base, *, messages=MESSAGES), which raises ParameterError for a window, a sample size or a minimum factor length out of range, a threshold outside (0, 1) or a logarithm base not above 1. Called before the words are extracted, it reports a wrong parameter before an empty text.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Some metrics depend on conventions that differ between libraries. All of them except the comparison with the MTLD threshold are class parameters:

Parameter Default Other libraries Logarithm base for Summer, Maas, Dugast's U and Dugast's k 10 LexicalRichness, textcomplexity and zipfR - natural MATTR window and MSTTR segment 50 quanteda and koRpus - 100 TTR threshold for MTLD 0.72 0.66-0.75 in the literature Comparison with the MTLD threshold a factor closes at TTR ≤ 0.72 (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010) lexical-diversity and TAALED - strict <; the values differ when TTR hits the threshold exactly Minimum MTLD factor length 10 koRpus - only in MTLD-MA, dropping shorter factors instead of extending them; LexicalRichness and textcomplexity - not applied HD-D sample size 42 35-50 in the literature

According to Zenker and Kyle (2021), MATTR, MTLD and HD-D are stable on texts of 50-200 words and longer, MTLD-W, MA-MTLD and Maas are unstable on short texts, and the TTR family never stabilizes. Texts of different lengths are compared by the windowed computation with confidence intervals.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description words tuple[str] Tuple of the words window_len, mtld_threshold, mtld_min_len, hdd_sample_size, log_base int/float Parameters of the metrics, changeable on the object frequency_spectrum dict[int, int] Frequency spectrum - the number of lexemes with a given frequency ttr float Type-Token Ratio (TTR) rttr float Root Type-Token Ratio (RTTR) cttr float Corrected Type-Token Ratio (CTTR) httr float Herdan Type-Token Ratio (HTTR) sttr float Summer Type-Token Ratio (STTR) mttr float Maas Type-Token Ratio (MTTR) dttr float Dugast Type-Token Ratio (DTTR) mattr float Moving Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR) msttr float Mean Segmental Type-Token Ratio (MSTTR) mtld float Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MTLD) mamtld float Moving Average Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MA-MTLD) mtldw float MTLD with a moving window and text wrap (MTLD-W) hdd float Hypergeometric Distribution D (HD-D) simpson_index float Simpson's index (D) inverse_simpson_index float Inverse Simpson's index (1/D) gini_simpson_index float Gini-Simpson index (1-D) hapax_index float Hapax index, a.k.a. Honoré's R honore_r float Alias for the hapax index yule_k float Yule's characteristic (Yule's K) yule_i float Inverse Yule's characteristic (Yule's I) herdan_vm float Herdan's Vm sichel_s float Sichel's S michea_m float Michéa's M brunet_w float Brunet's W dugast_k float Dugast's k baayen_p float Baayen's P hapax_ratio float Share of hapaxes among lexemes alpha2 float The α₂ exponent entropy float Shannon entropy in bits evenness float Evenness - the ratio of entropy to its maximum perplexity float Perplexity zipf_alpha float Zipf's law slope heaps_beta float Heaps' law exponent

Note

Every metric can also be computed by its function.

docs.title: windowed
docs.text:
Windowed computation of a metric by its name with calc_windowed: the mean of its values over consecutive windows of equal length, the sample standard deviation and the confidence interval of the mean. The edge cases (short texts, nan and infinite values) are described there.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description stat str - Metric name from get_stats window_len int 100 Window size step int None Window step, by default the window size (windows do not overlap) confidence float 0.95 Confidence level

Returns a WindowStats named tuple with the fields mean, std, lower, upper and n_windows. An unknown metric name raises UnknownStatError; a window size or a step that is not an integer of at least one and a confidence level that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

Example

from anyts import DiversityStats

ds = DiversityStats("a b c d e b c f g h g i g j k".split())
ds.windowed("ttr", window_len=5)
# WindowStats(mean=0.9333333333333332, std=0.11547005383792512, lower=0.6464898180167025, upper=1.220176848649964, n_windows=3)
ds.windowed("ttr", window_len=5, step=2).n_windows
# 6

docs.title: Metric functions
docs.text: Every function checks its words with check_words: a text that is a string, a Doc, an iterator, a set or a table, or whose words are not strings, raises SourceTypeError; fit_zipf_mandelbrot takes a counter too.

docs.title: Type-Token Ratio (TTR)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_ttr()

Computation of the Type-Token Ratio (TTR).

The simplest measure of lexical diversity; it is not corrected for text length.

Formula:

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Root Type-Token Ratio (RTTR)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_rttr()

Computation of the Root Type-Token Ratio (RTTR).

A modification of TTR (Guiraud, 1960).

Formula:

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}{\sqrt{\textrm{(Number of words)}}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Corrected Type-Token Ratio (CTTR)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_cttr()

Computation of the Corrected Type-Token Ratio (CTTR).

A modification of TTR (Carroll, 1964).

Formula:

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}{\sqrt{2\times\textrm{(Number of words)}}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Herdan Type-Token Ratio (HTTR)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_httr()

Computation of the Herdan Type-Token Ratio (HTTR).

A logarithmic modification of TTR (Herdan, 1960).

Formula:

\[ \frac{\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of lexemes)}}}{\log_{10} {{\textrm{(Number of words)}}}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Summer Type-Token Ratio (STTR)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_sttr()

Computation of the Summer Type-Token Ratio (STTR).

A logarithmic modification of TTR (Summer, 1966).

Note

The value depends on the logarithm base, 10 by default. See conventions. The value is nan for a text of one lexeme (the numerator is undefined) and for a text no longer than the base (\(\log \log N \le 0\)), including such windows of calc_windowed.

Formula:

\[ \frac{\log_{10} {\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of lexemes)}}}}{\log_{10} {\log_{10} {{\textrm{(Number of words)}}}}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Maas Type-Token Ratio (MTTR)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_mttr()

Computation of the Maas Type-Token Ratio (MTTR).

A logarithmic modification of TTR (Maas, 1972).

Note

The value depends on the logarithm base, 10 by default. See conventions.

Formula:

\[ \frac{\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of words)}}-\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of lexemes)}}}{\log_{10} {{\textrm{(Number of words)}}}^2} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Dugast Type-Token Ratio (DTTR)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_dttr()

Computation of the Dugast Type-Token Ratio (DTTR).

A logarithmic modification of TTR (Dugast, 1978), the reciprocal of the Maas metric.

Note

The value depends on the logarithm base, 10 by default. See conventions. A text without repeated words has an infinite value.

Formula:

\[ \frac{\log_{10} {{\textrm{(Number of words)}}}^2}{\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of words)}}-\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of lexemes)}}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Moving Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_mattr()

Computation of the Moving Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR).

A moving-average modification of TTR (Covington & McFall, 2010). Independent of text length.

Algorithm:

  1. Slide a fixed-size window over the text
  2. Compute TTR for every window
  3. Average the values

Note

For texts shorter than the window the TTR of the whole text is returned.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words window_len int 50 Window size (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN)

A window_len that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Mean Segmental Type-Token Ratio (MSTTR)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_msttr()

Computation of the Mean Segmental Type-Token Ratio (MSTTR).

A segmentation-based modification of TTR (Johnson, 1944). Independent of text length.

Algorithm:

  1. Split the text into fixed-size segments
  2. Compute TTR for every segment
  3. Average the values

Note

For texts shorter than the segment the TTR of the whole text is returned; an incomplete last segment is dropped.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words segment_len int 50 Segment size (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN)

A segment_len that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MTLD)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_mtld()

Computation of the Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MTLD).

A modification of MSTTR (McCarthy, 2005). Independent of text length.

Algorithm:

  1. The text is divided into factors - stretches on which TTR drops to the threshold 0.72 (TTR <= 0.72, see conventions)
  2. An incomplete last factor counts in proportion to how close its TTR came to the threshold
  3. The number of words is divided by the number of factors

The value is the mean of a forward and a backward pass (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010).

Note

The minimum factor length is non-standard (Kyle's lexical-diversity). If no factor completes and TTR never drops below 1, the value is infinity.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD)

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer and a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Moving Average Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MA-MTLD)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_mamtld()

Computation of the Moving Average Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MA-MTLD).

A moving-window modification of MTLD after MTLD-MA of koRpus: a factor starts at every position of the text, and the value is the mean length of the completed factors over a forward and a backward pass. koRpus makes the forward pass only, closes a factor at TTR strictly below the threshold and drops factors shorter than the minimum length instead of extending them.

Warning

If no factor completes, the function returns nan. The metric is unstable on short texts.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD)

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer and a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: MTLD with a moving window and text wrap (MTLD-W)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_mtldw()

Computation of MTLD-W (lexical-diversity mtld_ma_wrap, TAALED).

A modification of MA-MTLD: factors not completed by the end of the text continue from its beginning, so all positions get equal weight. A factor cannot be longer than the text.

Warning

If TTR does not drop to the threshold even over the whole text, the function returns nan. The metric is unstable on texts shorter than 100 words.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD)

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer and a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Hypergeometric Distribution D (HD-D)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_hdd()

Computation of the Hypergeometric Distribution D (HD-D).

An alternative to vocd-D (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010): the exact expected TTR of a random sample of sample_size words, without drawing samples. The hypergeometric distribution gives the probability that the sample holds each lexeme at least once; HD-D is the sum of these probabilities divided by the sample size.

Warning

For texts shorter than 50 words or than the sample size the metric is undefined; the function returns nan.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words sample_size int 42 Sample size in words (HDD_SAMPLE_SIZE)

A sample_size that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Simpson's index (D)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_simpson_index()

Computation of Simpson's index.

The probability that two words drawn from the text at random without replacement are the same lexeme. The lower the value, the richer the vocabulary.

Warning

For texts shorter than two words the index is undefined; the function returns nan. The same holds for the inverse Simpson's index and the Gini-Simpson index.

Formula:

\[ \frac{\sum n\times(n-1)}{\textrm{(Number of words)}\times(\textrm{Number of words}-1)} \]

where \(n\) is the number of occurrences of a lexeme in the text.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Inverse Simpson's index (1/D)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_inverse_simpson_index()

Computation of the inverse Simpson's index, an estimate of the Hill number of order two (\(1/\sum_k p_k^2\)) from pairs drawn without replacement.

The higher the value, the richer the vocabulary.

Formula:

\[ \frac{1}{D} \]

Warning

If all words of the text are unique, Simpson's index is 0 and the inverse index is infinity.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Gini-Simpson index (1-D)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_gini_simpson_index()

Computation of the Gini-Simpson index.

The probability that two randomly chosen words of the text are different. The higher the value, the richer the vocabulary.

Formula:

\[ 1-D \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Hapax index (Honoré's R)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_hapax_index(), alias anyts.diversity_stats.calc_honore_r()

Computation of the hapax index.

Definition

A hapax (Greek ἅπαξ λεγόμενον - "said only once") is a word that occurs only once in a corpus. For instance, baciyelmo, Sancho Panza's word for the barber's basin that Don Quixote takes for a helmet, is a hapax of Cervantes (chapter 44 of the first part of Don Quixote).

The metric coincides with Honoré's measure (1979), with the natural logarithm.

Formula:

\[ 100\times\frac{\ln {\textrm{(Number of words)}}}{1-\frac{\textrm{Number of hapaxes}}{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}} \]

Warning

If all words of the text are hapaxes, the index is infinity. For texts shorter than two words the index is undefined; the function returns nan.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Frequency spectrum
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_frequency_spectrum()

Computation of the frequency spectrum - the number of lexemes \(V_i\) occurring exactly \(i\) times in the text. The hapax index, Yule's K and I, Herdan's Vm, Sichel's S, Michéa's M, Baayen's P, the hapax ratio and the α₂ exponent are computed from it, with the formulas of Tweedie and Baayen (1998).

Notation: \(N\) - number of words, \(V\) - number of lexemes, \(V_i\) - number of lexemes with frequency \(i\), \(V_1\) - hapaxes, \(V_2\) - dis legomena, \(p_k\) - relative frequency of a lexeme.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Yule's characteristic (Yule's K)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_yule_k()

Computation of Yule's characteristic (Yule, 1944). One of the few measures theoretically independent of text length (Tweedie & Baayen, 1998); in practice it converges as the text grows. The lower the value, the richer the vocabulary. Proportional to Simpson's index: \(K \approx 10^4 \cdot D\).

Formula:

\[ K = 10^4\times\frac{\sum_i i^2 V_i - N}{N^2} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Inverse Yule's characteristic (Yule's I)
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_yule_i()

Computation of the inverse Yule's characteristic. The higher the value, the richer the vocabulary; if all words of the text are unique, the value is infinity.

Formula:

\[ I = \frac{V^2}{\sum_i i^2 V_i - V} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Herdan's Vm
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_herdan_vm()

Computation of Herdan's measure (Herdan, 1955). Theoretically independent of text length; the lower the value, the richer the vocabulary.

Formula:

\[ V_m = \sqrt{\sum_i V_i \left(\frac{i}{N}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{V}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Sichel's S
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_sichel_s()

Computation of Sichel's measure (Sichel, 1975) - the share of dis legomena, lexemes with frequency 2, among all lexemes. Stable across texts of different lengths.

Formula:

\[ S = \frac{V_2}{V} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Michéa's M
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_michea_m()

Computation of Michéa's measure (Michéa, 1969) - the reciprocal of Sichel's measure. If the text has no dis legomena, the value is infinity.

Formula:

\[ M = \frac{V}{V_2} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Brunet's W
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_brunet_w()

Computation of Brunet's measure (Brunet, 1978). Values for texts usually lie within 10-20; the lower the value, the richer the vocabulary.

Formula:

\[ W = N^{V^{-a}}, \quad a = 0.172 \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words a float 0.172 Exponent (BRUNET_W_EXPONENT)

An a that is not a finite number raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Dugast's k
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_dugast_k()

Computation of Dugast's measure (Dugast, 1979). Not to be confused with Dugast's U - the DTTR metric.

Note

The value depends on the logarithm base, 10 by default. For texts no longer than the base (\(\log N \le 1\)) the measure is undefined; the function returns nan.

Formula:

\[ k = \frac{\log V}{\log \log N} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Baayen's P
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_baayen_p()

Computation of Baayen's measure (Baayen, 1991) - the share of hapaxes among all words of the text. Equals the slope of the vocabulary growth curve at the end of the text: the probability that the next word is new (Evert, 2004).

Formula:

\[ P = \frac{V_1}{N} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Hapax ratio
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_hapax_ratio()

Computation of the share of hapaxes among all lexemes of the text.

Formula:

\[ \frac{V_1}{V} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: The α₂ exponent
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_alpha2()

Computation of the exponent \(\alpha_2\) - an estimate of the Zipf-Mandelbrot parameter from the lower part of the frequency spectrum (Evert, 2004). If the text has no hapaxes, the function returns nan.

Formula:

\[ \alpha_2 = 1 - \frac{2 V_2}{V_1} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Shannon entropy
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_entropy()

Computation of the Shannon entropy of the lexeme distribution in bits. The higher the value, the richer the vocabulary. The Hill number of order one is \(2^H\) (perplexity), of order zero - \(V\); the inverse Simpson's index estimates the one of order two.

Formula:

\[ H = -\sum_k p_k \log_2 p_k \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Evenness
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_evenness()

Computation of evenness (Pielou's evenness) - the ratio of the Shannon entropy to its maximum for the given number of lexemes. Ranges from 0 to 1; for texts of a single lexeme it is undefined, the function returns nan.

Formula:

\[ \frac{H}{\log_2 V} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Perplexity
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_perplexity()

Computation of perplexity - the Hill number of order one, the effective number of lexemes of the text.

Formula:

\[ 2^H \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Zipf's law slope
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_zipf_alpha()

Computation of the exponent \(\alpha\) of Zipf's law \(f(r) \propto r^{-\alpha}\), where \(r\) is the frequency rank of a lexeme. Estimated by linear regression of log frequency on log rank. For natural texts \(\alpha\) is close to 1.

Note

The rank-based least squares estimate is biased; maximum likelihood is more accurate. For texts of a single lexeme the function returns nan.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Zipf-Mandelbrot fit
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.fit_zipf_mandelbrot(), anyts.diversity_stats.ZipfMandelbrot

Fitting the Zipf-Mandelbrot law \(f(r) = C / (r + q)^s\) to the rank-frequency distribution. With \(q = 0\) it is Zipf's law with exponent \(s\); the shift \(q\) captures the flattening of the curve on the most frequent words. Fitted by least squares in logarithmic coordinates with \(q \ge 0\), \(s \ge 0\). Returns a ZipfMandelbrot named tuple with the fields c, q, s and r2 - the coefficient of determination of the fit in logarithmic coordinates.

Note

All fields are nan for texts of fewer than three lexemes, with identical frequencies of all lexemes or when the fit diverges. The parameters are unstable on short texts: the law describes large corpora.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str]/Counter - List of words or a counter of their frequencies

A counter whose words are not strings or whose frequencies are not numbers raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite frequency SourceError (check_counts).

Example

from anyts.diversity_stats import fit_zipf_mandelbrot

# the frequencies 12, 6, 4, 3 follow the law f = 12 / r exactly
words = ["a"] * 12 + ["b"] * 6 + ["c"] * 4 + ["d"] * 3
fit = fit_zipf_mandelbrot(words)
round(fit.c, 3), round(fit.q, 3), round(fit.s, 3), round(fit.r2, 3)
# (12.001, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0)

docs.title: Heaps' law exponent
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_heaps_beta(), anyts.diversity_stats.fit_heaps(), anyts.diversity_stats.vocabulary_growth()

Computation of the exponent \(\beta\) of Heaps' law \(V(N) = K \cdot N^{\beta}\) of vocabulary growth with text length, estimated by linear regression of log vocabulary size on log text length along the growth curve. On corpora of millions of words \(\beta\) lies within 0.4-0.6, on a single text within 0.6-0.9, so the values are comparable only between texts of similar length.

Note

The value depends on word order and needs several hundred words or more. For texts shorter than two words the function returns nan.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

vocabulary_growth returns the vocabulary growth curve: the vocabulary size after every word of the text.

fit_heaps fits the law over this curve and returns a HeapsFit named tuple with the parameters k, beta and the coefficient of determination r2.

docs.title: Windowed computation
docs.text:
anyts.diversity_stats.calc_windowed()

Windowed computation of any metric: the mean of its values over consecutive windows of equal length, their sample standard deviation and the confidence interval of the mean by Student's distribution. The standard way to compare texts of different lengths; Kubát and Milička's standardized TTR (not Summer's STTR) is a windowed TTR with a 1000-word window and a 95% interval. A text shorter than the window is a single window; nan windows are ignored. A metric infinite in any window (e.g. the inverse Simpson's index on a window of unique words) makes the mean infinite and the deviation and the interval nan. Returns a WindowStats named tuple with the fields mean, std, lower, upper and n_windows.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words func callable - Function computing the metric from a list of words window_len int 100 Window size step int None Window step, by default equal to the window size confidence float 0.95 Confidence level messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key, a keyword

A func that cannot be called raises SourceTypeError; a window_len or a step that is not an integer of at least one and a confidence that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Lexical sophistication
docs.text: anyts.lexical_stats.LexicalStats, anyts.lexical_stats.calc_surprisal()

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Lexical sophistication in the manner of TAALES (Kyle, Crossley and Berger, 2018) - how rare the words of a text are: the mean frequency, range and dispersion of the words by a frequency dictionary, the surprisal and the perplexity by its unigram model, the shares of the frequency bands of a list of the most frequent lemmas and the lexical density, the share of the content words. The statistics by the dictionary are computed when first read, so the bands and the lexical density need no dictionary data.

A dictionary of another class than that of the library raises SourceTypeError, a source without words SourceError.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text:
A language library subclasses LexicalStats:

Hook Kind Description analyze(source) method The words of a source as LexicalWord: the word, its lemma and whether it is a content word; an abstract method. Numbers (is_number of anyts.utils) are not words freq_dict_class class attribute Class of the frequency dictionary, made without arguments when none is given; a dictionary of another class is refused dictionary_keys() method Keys of the words in the dictionary; the lemmas by default, or for instance a proper noun by its form rank(lemma) method Rank of a lemma in the list of the most frequent lemmas, None out of it; no list by default top_size() method Size of the list, the upper bound of band_coverage; 10000 by default stats_desc, stats_headers class attributes Statistics of get_stats with their descriptions (anyts.constants.LEXICAL_STATS_DESC by default), headers of the columns for print_stats messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

A library takes its own parameters, such as a pipeline or a word extractor, in its __init__ and passes the source and the dictionary on. An analyze that does not give LexicalWord objects raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Frequency dictionary
docs.text:
The dictionary is any object of the protocol FrequencyDictionary: lookup(lemma) gives the entry of a lemma or None, ipm(lemma) its frequency per million words or 0, and min_ipm the lowest frequency of the dictionary, above zero. An entry (FrequencyEntry) has the frequency ipm, above zero, the range range (the parts of the corpus with the lemma) and the dispersion dispersion. Without freq_dict_class a dictionary without lookup and ipm raises SourceTypeError.

FrequencyEntry is the entry of a lemma in a FrequencyDictionary: ipm, range and dispersion.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description source str/Doc - Data source freq_dict FrequencyDictionary None Frequency dictionary; freq_dict_class() by default

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description words, lemmas tuple[str] Words and their lemmas; the bands are counted by the lemmas keys tuple[str] Keys of the words in the dictionary entries tuple[FrequencyEntry or None] Entries of the dictionary, None for a word out of it ranks tuple[int or None] Ranks of the lemmas, None out of the list n_words, n_content_words, n_found int Number of words, of content words and of words found in the dictionary coverage float Share of words found in the dictionary mean_ipm, mean_ipm_content float Mean frequency of the words found, of the content words found mean_log_ipm, mean_log_ipm_content float Mean decimal logarithm of the frequency, of the words found and of the content words found mean_range, mean_dispersion float Mean range and dispersion of the words found surprisal, perplexity float Mean surprisal in bits (calc_surprisal), 2 to its power p_top1000, p_top2000, p_top5000, p_top10000, p_beyond_top10000 float Shares of the words with a lemma in the top 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 of the list and beyond it lexical_density float Share of content words

A mean over no words found is nan, and so is a band beyond the size of the list (top_size).

docs.title: band_coverage
docs.text:
band_coverage(bands, unique) gives the share of the words with a lemma in the top N of the list for every bound N of bands (FREQUENCY_BANDS by default), or with unique=True the share of the distinct lemmas. Bounds that are not a list of integers or a bound out of 1 and top_size() raise ParameterError.

The other methods - get_stats, to_dataframe, print_stats and describe - are those of the statistics interface.

docs.title: calc_surprisal
docs.text:
The mean surprisal of the words by the unigram model of a frequency dictionary, in bits; a word out of the dictionary gets its lowest frequency min_ipm. The perplexity is 2 to its power.

Formula:

\[ \frac{1}{N} \sum_{w} -\log_2 \frac{\max(\textrm{ipm}_w, \textrm{min\_ipm})}{10^6} \] Parameter Type Default Description lemmas list[str] - Keys of the words in the dictionary freq_dict FrequencyDictionary - Frequency dictionary

No words give nan; keys that are not a list of strings and a dictionary without ipm and min_ipm raise SourceTypeError, a lowest frequency that is not above zero ParameterError.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

from typing import NamedTuple

from anyts.lexical_stats import LexicalStats, LexicalWord


class Entry(NamedTuple):
    ipm: float
    range: int
    dispersion: float


class Frequencies:
    min_ipm = 0.5
    entries = {"the": Entry(50000.0, 40, 0.99), "cat": Entry(100.0, 38, 0.9)}

    def lookup(self, lemma):
        return self.entries.get(lemma)

    def ipm(self, lemma):
        entry = self.lookup(lemma)
        return entry.ipm if entry is not None else 0.0


class Lexical(LexicalStats):
    freq_dict_class = Frequencies

    def analyze(self, source):
        return [LexicalWord(word, word.lower(), word.lower() != "the") for word in source.split()]


stats = Lexical("The cat purrs")
stats.coverage, round(stats.mean_log_ipm, 3), round(stats.surprisal, 3)
# (0.6666666666666666, 3.349, 12.847)

docs.title: Phonetic statistics
docs.text: anyts.phon_stats.PhonStats

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The phonetic statistics of a text: the shares of the vowels, the sonorants and the voiced and voiceless obstruents, the ratio of the consonants to the vowels, the consonant clusters, the hiatuses, the entropy of the CV patterns of the words, the hardness, the alliteration and the assonance, the open syllables and the mean length of a syllable. A sound is a letter of a word by default, or a sound of its transcription when a library gives one. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy; the words are taken in lower case, and an extractor passed explicitly is used on the text of a Doc.

A source that is neither a string nor a Doc and an extractor of another type raise SourceTypeError, a source without words SourceError, a window that is not an integer of at least 2 ParameterError.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text:
A language library subclasses PhonStats:

Hook Kind Description vowels, sonorants, voiced, voiceless class attributes Classes of the sounds - the vowels, the sonorants and the voiced and voiceless obstruents; the last three are the consonants. The classes and skipped must not overlap, checked when the class is defined skipped class attribute Sounds that neither count nor break a consonant cluster, such as a sign that marks the consonant before it glides class attribute Vowels that make no hiatus after a vowel, such as a letter that writes a glide and a vowel transcribe(word) method Sounds of a word; its letters by default syllabify(word) method Syllables of a word as it writes them; an abstract method syllable_sounds(word) method Sounds of every syllable of a word; the transcription of every syllable of syllabify by default word_hiatus(word) method Number of the hiatuses of a word; its runs of vowels by count_hiatus with glides by default, or for instance the vowels at the boundaries of its syllables doc_words(doc) method Words of a Doc; those of iter_doc_words in lower case by default words_extractor_class, join_hyphens class attributes Word extractor of a string, joining of the hyphenated words of a Doc stats_desc, stats_headers class attributes Statistics of get_stats with their descriptions (anyts.constants.PHON_STATS_DESC by default), headers of the columns for print_stats messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

Classes of sounds that are not collections of strings raise SourceTypeError when the class is defined, and a syllabify or a transcribe that does not return strings raises it when the statistics are computed.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description source str/Doc - Data source words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool; used for a Doc too, on its text window_len int 3 Window in words of the alliteration and the assonance (PHON_WINDOW_LEN)

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description words tuple[str] Words in lower case window_len int Window of the alliteration and the assonance syllables, sounds tuple Syllables (syllabify) and sounds (transcribe) of every word n_vowels, n_sonorants, n_voiced, n_voiceless, n_consonants int Numbers of the sounds by class c_clusters dict[int, int] Number of the consonant clusters by length (consonant_clusters) c_syllable_patterns dict[str, int] Number of the syllables by CV pattern; a syllable without a sound of the classes (a number) is no syllable p_vowels, p_sonorants, p_voiced, p_voiceless float Shares of the sounds by class consonant_vowel_ratio float Ratio of the consonants to the vowels p_heavy_clusters float Share of the clusters of three consonants or more p_hiatus float Hiatuses per word cv_entropy float Shannon entropy of the CV patterns of the words, in bits hardness float Voiceless consonants to the vowels and the sonorants alliteration, assonance float Repetition index of the consonants and of the vowels (calc_repetition_index) p_open_syllables float Share of the syllables that end in a vowel mean_syllable_len float Mean length of a syllable in sounds

A share or a ratio without sounds, clusters or syllables to divide by is nan, and so are the hiatuses per word and the entropy of a text without sounds.

The methods get_stats, to_dataframe, print_stats and describe are those of the statistics interface.

docs.title: Metric functions
docs.text: The metrics and their functions are described in the metric functions section.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

import re

from anyts.phon_stats import PhonStats


class Phon(PhonStats):
    vowels = frozenset("aeiou")
    sonorants = frozenset("lmnrwy")
    voiced = frozenset("bdgvz")
    voiceless = frozenset("cfhkpqstx")

    def syllabify(self, word):
        return re.findall(r"[^aeiou]*[aeiou]+(?:[^aeiou]+$)?", word) or [word]


stats = Phon("The poet sat on a stone by the stream")
stats.c_clusters, stats.p_hiatus
# ({1: 7, 2: 4, 3: 1}, 0.2222222222222222)

docs.title: Metric functions
docs.text: The functions know no language: a word is given as its letters (the characters of a string) or the sounds of its transcription, and the classes of the sounds or the features to count come through the parameters.

docs.title: CV pattern
docs.text:
anyts.phon_stats.cv_pattern()

The CV pattern of a word or a syllable: V for a vowel, C for a consonant, the other sounds (signs, digits, letters of another script) left out.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description sounds list[str] - Sounds or letters of the word vowels Collection[str] - Vowels consonants Collection[str] - Consonants

docs.title: Consonant clusters
docs.text:
anyts.phon_stats.consonant_clusters()

The lengths of the consonant clusters of a word in order: a cluster is a run of consonants, a single one included; a sound of skipped neither counts nor breaks the run, any other sound breaks it.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description sounds list[str] - Sounds or letters of the word consonants Collection[str] - Consonants skipped Collection[str] () Sounds that keep a cluster whole, such as a sign that marks the consonant before it

docs.title: Hiatuses
docs.text:
anyts.phon_stats.count_hiatus()

The number of the hiatuses of a word by its vowels in a row: a run of two vowels or more is one hiatus; a vowel of glides after a vowel makes none.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description sounds list[str] - Sounds or letters of the word vowels Collection[str] - Vowels glides Collection[str] () Vowels that make no hiatus after a vowel, such as a letter that writes a glide and a vowel

docs.title: Repetition index
docs.text:
anyts.phon_stats.calc_repetition_index()

The repetition index: the number of windows of window_len neighbouring words where a feature (a letter or a sound) occurs in two words or more, summed over the features, divided by the number expected if the words stood in random order. A window of shuffled words is a sample without replacement, so for a feature found in \(K\) of the \(N\) words, a window of \(w\) words holds it in two words or more with the hypergeometric probability

\[ P = 1 - \frac{\binom{N-K}{w} + K \binom{N-K}{w-1}}{\binom{N}{w}} \]

and the expected number is the sum of these probabilities over the features times the \(N - w + 1\) windows. Since the expectation comes from the text itself, the index shows whether the repetitions gather in neighbouring words, not how frequent a feature is: it averages to 1 over the orders of the words and is well above 1 when the repetitions come closer than chance. A word counts a feature once; the index is nan for a text shorter than the window or with no feature shared by two words.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str]/list[list[str]] - Features of every word: a string of its letters or a collection of its sounds window_len int - Window in words, at least 2 features Collection[str] None Features to count, all of them by default

Words that are not a list of strings or of collections of strings and features that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, and a window_len that is not an integer of at least 2 ParameterError.

from anyts.phon_stats import calc_repetition_index, consonant_clusters, count_hiatus, cv_pattern

vowels, consonants = set("aeiou"), set("bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxyz")
cv_pattern("strong", vowels, consonants)
# 'CCCVCC'

# (3, 4)

docs.title: Readability metrics
docs.text: anyts.readability_stats.ReadabilityStats

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The readability metrics of a text from its basic statistics: the mean sentence length in words, the mean word length in syllables or letters, the share of polysyllabic and of long words and the variability of word length. The data source is a text, a Doc object of spaCy or ready basic statistics, which are reused as they are; the extractors are passed on to the basic statistics of a text or a Doc. The formulas count only the letters of the counted words, so a word extractor that drops words does not lengthen the mean word.

The metrics are properties computed on each access, so a change of the coefficients of an object applies at once.

A source that is neither a string, a Doc nor basic statistics, basic statistics of a class other than those of the library and an extractor of another type raise SourceTypeError, a source without words or sentences SourceError, an unknown preset or one that is not a string ParameterError.

that of preset_level_scales, else of level_scales by default grade_scales class attribute Scales of a metric in years of schooling for describe, as lower bounds and grades; a scale of bands comes first, so a metric read by years of schooling stays out of level_scales and preset_level_scales reading_speed, reading_speed_norms class attributes Reading speed of reading_time and the speeds of the norms, words per minute; READING_SPEED_WPM and READING_SPEED_NORMS by default reading_ease_grades class attribute Scale of the reading ease in years of schooling for the consensus grade, as lower bounds and grades, the lowest band open below preset_reading_ease_grades class attribute Scales of reading_ease_grades by preset, in its place for the preset reading_ease_to_grade(flesch_reading_easy) method Years of schooling for the reading ease in the consensus grade; the band of the scale of the preset in preset_reading_ease_grades, else of reading_ease_grades by default messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

A formula of the library is a property of the subclass named in stats_desc, and in grade_stats when it gives years of schooling; its coefficients may live in the presets under its name. The preset is a parameter: a library sets its own default in its __init__ and passes it on. When the class is defined, ParameterError is raised by a preset unknown to presets among the keys of preset_level_scales or preset_reading_ease_grades, by a scale of them, of grade_scales or of reading_ease_grades that is not one of scale_level with finite grades, by grade_age_levels that are not quadruples of the first and the last year, the stage and the age in ascending order of the years, and by a postgraduate_level that is not a pair of strings.

The core defaults are the original English formulas: the preset original of anyts.constants.READABILITY_PRESETS, the grade formulas Flesch-Kincaid, Coleman-Liau, ARI, SMOG and Gunning fog, polysyllabic words of three syllables and long words of seven letters, the school stages of the United States, the scales of the reading ease, LIX and RIX, the years of schooling of the reading ease of text_standard of textstat (READING_EASE_GRADES, 13 below 30), and the reading speed of 238 words per minute with the norm adult - 183 words per minute aloud and 238 silently (Brysbaert, 2019).

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
A subclass with the basic statistics of a language - here the syllables are the groups of vowels, a rough rule for English.

Example

import re

from anyts.basic_stats import BasicStats
from anyts.readability_stats import ReadabilityStats


class Stats(BasicStats):
    def count_syllables(self, word):
        return len(re.findall(r"[aeiouy]+", word, re.IGNORECASE))


class Readability(ReadabilityStats):
    basic_stats_class = Stats


rs = Readability("The cat sat on the mat. A beautiful day!")
round(rs.flesch_reading_easy, 2), round(rs.flesch_kincaid_grade, 2)
# (98.87, 0.59)
rs.consensus_grade, rs.describe_grade()
# (3.0, 'elementary school, grades 1-5 (6-11 years)')
rs.describe("flesch_reading_easy"), rs.describe("lix"), rs.describe("mu_index")
# ('5th grade', "very easy texts, children's books", None)
rs.reading_time_by_norm("adult")
# (0.04918032786885246, 0.037815126050420166)

docs.title: Metric functions
docs.text: The coefficients of the formulas are parameters; the defaults below are those of the original English formulas. A formula of counts gives nan when the number of words or of sentences it divides by is zero.

docs.title: Flesch reading ease
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.calc_flesch_reading_easy()

Computation of the Flesch reading ease (Flesch, 1948).

The higher the value, the easier the text: nominally 0 to 100, though the simplest texts go above 100 and the hardest below 0.

Formula:

\[ c - a \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} - b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of syllables}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 1.015 Coefficient a, at the mean sentence length b float 84.6 Coefficient b, at the mean word length c float 206.835 Coefficient c, the constant

docs.title: Flesch-Kincaid grade
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.calc_flesch_kincaid_grade()

Computation of the Flesch-Kincaid grade (Kincaid et al., 1975).

The years of schooling needed to read the text; the higher the value, the harder the text.

Formula:

\[ a \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} + b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of syllables}}{\textrm{Number of words}} - c \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 0.39 Coefficient a, at the mean sentence length b float 11.8 Coefficient b, at the mean word length c float 15.59 Coefficient c, the constant

docs.title: Coleman-Liau index
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.calc_coleman_liau_index()

Computation of the Coleman-Liau index (Coleman and Liau, 1975).

The years of schooling needed to read the text from the letters and the sentences per 100 words; the higher the value, the harder the text.

Formula:

\[ a \cdot \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of letters}}{\textrm{Number of words}} - b \cdot \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of sentences}}{\textrm{Number of words}} - c \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description n_letters int - Number of letters of the words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 0.0588 Coefficient a, at the letters per 100 words b float 0.296 Coefficient b, at the sentences per 100 words c float 15.8 Coefficient c, the constant

docs.title: Automated readability index (ARI)
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.calc_automated_readability_index()

Computation of the automated readability index (Smith and Senter, 1967).

The years of schooling needed to read the text from the letters per word and the words per sentence; the higher the value, the harder the text.

Formula:

\[ a \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of letters}}{\textrm{Number of words}} + b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} - c \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description n_letters int - Number of letters of the words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 4.71 Coefficient a, at the letters per word b float 0.5 Coefficient b, at the mean sentence length c float 21.43 Coefficient c, the constant

docs.title: SMOG index
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.calc_smog_index()

Computation of the SMOG index (McLaughlin, 1969).

The years of schooling needed to read the text from the polysyllabic words per sentence; the higher the value, the harder the text. In the original formula the polysyllabic words have three or more syllables and b brings their number to a sample of 30 sentences.

Formula:

\[ a \cdot \sqrt{b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of polysyllabic words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}}} + c \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description n_complex int - Number of polysyllabic words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 1.043 Coefficient a, at the square root b float 30 Coefficient b, the number of sentences of the sample c float 3.1291 Coefficient c, the constant

docs.title: Gunning fog index
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.calc_gunning_fog_index()

Computation of the Gunning fog index (Gunning, 1952).

The years of schooling needed to read the text from the mean sentence length and the percentage of complex words, in the original formula the words of three or more syllables; the higher the value, the harder the text.

Formula:

\[ a \cdot \left(\frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} + \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of complex words}}{\textrm{Number of words}}\right) \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description n_complex int - Number of complex words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 0.4 Coefficient a

docs.title: LIX readability index
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.calc_lix()

Computation of the LIX readability index (Björnsson, 1968).

The mean sentence length plus the percentage of long words, the words of more than six letters; there are no coefficients to fit. The higher the value, the harder the text:

Value Text 0-30 very easy texts, children's books 30-40 easy texts, fiction, newspaper articles 40-50 texts of medium difficulty, magazine articles 50-60 hard texts, popular science, official texts 60-100 very hard texts, laws and bureaucratic language

Formula:

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} + \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of long words}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description n_long_words int - Number of long words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences

docs.title: RIX readability index
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.calc_rix()

Computation of the RIX readability index (Anderson, 1983).

The long words, of more than six letters, per sentence; there are no coefficients to fit. The higher the value, the harder the text:

Value Grade < 0.2 1 0.2-0.5 2 0.5-0.8 3 0.8-1.3 4 1.3-1.8 5 1.8-2.4 6 2.4-3.0 7 3.0-3.7 8 3.7-4.5 9 4.5-5.3 10 5.3-6.2 11 6.2-7.2 12 > 7.2 college

Formula:

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of long words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description n_long_words int - Number of long words n_sents int - Number of sentences

docs.title: Legibilidad µ
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.calc_mu_index()

Computation of Legibilidad µ (Muñoz Baquedano and Muñoz Urra, 2006).

The mean number of letters per word divided by its sample variance, times 100; there are no coefficients to fit, and the higher the value, the easier the text. Words without letters (numbers) are left out; with fewer than two words or without variability the index is undefined (nan).

Formula:

\[ 100 \cdot \frac{\bar{x}}{s^2}, \quad s^2 = \frac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1} \]

where \(x_i\) is the number of letters of a word and \(n\) the number of words.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description c_letters dict[int, int] - Distribution of words by number of letters

A c_letters that is not a mapping raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Reading ease as a grade
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.flesch_reading_easy_to_grade()

Conversion of the Flesch reading ease into years of schooling for the consensus grade: the grade of the first band whose lower bound the value reaches, or below under the last bound; values above 100 belong to the first band. A reading ease or a below that is not a finite number raises ParameterError, and so do grades that are empty or not pairs of finite numbers with descending bounds.

The default bands are those of text_standard of textstat, which follow the table of Flesch (1948) down to 60 and split his lower bands, with 8.5 for its grades 8 and 9: 90-100 - 5, 80-90 - 6, 70-80 - 7, 60-70 - 8.5, 50-60 - 10, 40-50 - 11, 30-40 - 12, below 30 - 13 (anyts.constants.READING_EASE_GRADES).

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description flesch_reading_easy float - Value of the reading ease grades list[tuple[float, float]] READING_EASE_GRADES Lower bounds and their grades in descending order of the bounds below float 13 Grade below the last bound

docs.title: Consensus grade
docs.text:
anyts.readability_stats.calc_consensus_grade()

Computation of the consensus grade: the median of the values of the grade formulas rounded half up, together with the reading ease in years of schooling by to_grade, not rounded - so a band of 8.5 votes for 8.5. No values at all, a grade or a reading ease that is not a finite number raise ParameterError, a to_grade that is not callable SourceTypeError.

Parameters:

docs.title: School stage and age

anyts.readability_stats.grade_to_age()

The school stage and reader age by the value of a grade formula: the value is rounded half up and falls into the first stage whose last year it does not exceed, values below 1 into the first stage; above the last stage lies above. A grade that is not a finite number raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Statistics interface
docs.text: anyts.stats.Stats

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The common interface of the classes of statistics: the dictionary of the statistics, nested or flat, a one-row frame of pandas, a printed table with descriptions and the reading of a statistic by its scale. Every class of statistics is built on it, those of a language library too.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
A class of statistics subclasses Stats:

Hook Kind Description stats_desc class attribute Statistics of the class with their descriptions; each is an attribute or a property of the object stat_names() method Names of the statistics of get_stats; the keys of stats_desc by default stats_headers class attribute Headers of the columns for print_stats; ("Statistic", "Value") by default level_scales class attribute Interpretation scales of describe by statistic, as lower bounds and their bands in descending order; none by default level_scale(stat) method Interpretation scale of a statistic; level_scales by default, overridden when the scale depends on the parameters of the object messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default, checked when the class is defined

docs.title: get_stats
docs.text:
Returns a copy of the statistics of stat_names: editing it does not change the object. With flat=True the values of a dictionary statistic become keys of their own, joined to its name with an underscore: the distribution {3: 5} of c_lengths gives the key c_lengths_3.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description flat bool False Turn the values of the dictionary statistics into keys of their own

docs.title: to_dataframe
docs.text: Returns the flat statistics, get_stats(flat=True), as a pandas.DataFrame of one row with a column for every key. A dictionary statistic gives columns only for the keys the text has, so in frames of several texts joined with pandas.concat a count a text lacks is NaN. Only these columns may be filled with 0: elsewhere NaN is an undefined value.
