docs.text: Prints a table of the statistics of stats_desc with their descriptions under the headers of stats_headers, floats with two decimals; each column is as wide as its longest text.

docs.title: describe
docs.text:
Returns the band of the scale of a statistic (level_scale), and None for a statistic without a scale or with an undefined value (nan). A name that is neither of stat_names nor a public property of the class raises UnknownStatError.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description stat str - Name of the statistic

The band is found by scale_level; ReadabilityStats also reads the grade formulas by school stages.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

from anyts.stats import Stats


class TextSize(Stats):
    stats_desc = {"n_words": "Words", "c_lengths": "Words by length"}
    level_scales = {"n_words": ((100, "long"), (0, "short"))}

    def __init__(self, text):
        words = text.split()
        self.n_words = len(words)
        self.c_lengths = {3: sum(len(word) == 3 for word in words)}


size = TextSize("The cat sat on the mat")
size.get_stats(flat=True)
# {'n_words': 6, 'c_lengths_3': 5}
size.describe("n_words")
# 'short'
size.print_stats()
#    Statistic    |  Value
# ---------------------------
# Words           |    6
# Words by length |  {3: 5}

docs.title: Style metrics
docs.text: anyts.style_stats.StyleStats

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The style metrics of a text: the SEO metrics of Advego and Text.ru - the classic and the academic nausea, the water content, the spam score, the naturalness by Zipf's law and the keyword density - and the markers of the officialese style: the verbal nouns, the compound prepositions, the parenthetical expressions and the cliches. The services publish no formulas, so the common definitions are taken, as the metric functions give them. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy.

The SEO metrics are counted on the words of the word extractor, in lower case by default, or on the tokens of a Doc; an extractor passed explicitly is used on the text of a Doc. The markers are counted on the word forms in lower case (forms), whatever the extractor.

A source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type and a list that is not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, a source without words SourceError, a top_n that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

Returns the markers of the officialese found by metric - verbal_nouns, compound_prepositions, parentheticals, cliches - as the forms write them, in the order of the text.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

from anyts.style_stats import StyleStats


class Style(StyleStats):
    cliches_list = ("make a decision",)

    def is_stopword(self, word):
        return word in {"the", "and", "a", "to"}


style = Style("The board will make a decision and the board will vote")
style.academic_nausea, style.water, style.cliches
# (63.63636363636363, 36.36363636363637, 9.090909090909092)
style.markers()["cliches"]
# ('make a decision',)

docs.title: Metric functions
docs.text: The services publish no formulas, so the common definitions are taken. The language - the stopwords, the water, the normalized form of a word, the spelling of phrases - comes through the keyword parameters; words, stopwords, keywords and phrases that are not a list of strings and hooks that cannot be called raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Classic nausea
docs.text:
anyts.style_stats.calc_classic_nausea()

Computation of the classic nausea (Advego): how much one word is pressed. Not corrected for text length, it grows with the text; no words give 0.

Formula:

\[ \sqrt{f_1} \]

where \(f_1\) is the number of occurrences of the most frequent word.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Words of the academic nausea
docs.text:
anyts.style_stats.find_nausea_words()

The top_n most frequent words without the stopwords, with their occurrences: the most frequent first, words of equal frequency in the order of the text. A stopword is a word of stopwords by its normalized form or, without the list, a word is_stopword accepts; without both there are no stopwords.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words (NAUSEA_TOP_N) stopwords list[str] None Stopwords is_stopword Callable None Whether a word is a stopword, without the list normalize Callable str.lower Normalized form of a word messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

A top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Academic nausea
docs.text:
anyts.style_stats.calc_academic_nausea()

Computation of the academic nausea (Advego): the share of the occurrences of the most frequent significant words (find_nausea_words) among all the words, in percent. With the stopwords, the most frequent words of any text would be its conjunctions and prepositions.

Formula:

\[ 100 \cdot \frac{\sum_{w \in \textrm{top}_n} f_w}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words (NAUSEA_TOP_N) stopwords list[str] None Stopwords is_stopword Callable None Whether a word is a stopword, without the list normalize Callable str.lower Normalized form of a word messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

A top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Water content
docs.text:
anyts.style_stats.calc_water()

Computation of the water content (Text.ru): the share of the words without content, in percent - the words of stopwords by their normalized forms or, without the list, those is_water_word accepts.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words stopwords list[str] None Words of water is_water_word Callable None Whether a word is water, without the list normalize Callable str.lower Normalized form of a word

docs.title: Spam score
docs.text:
anyts.style_stats.calc_spam()

Computation of the spam score (Text.ru): the share of the repeated words in percent, every occurrence of a word after the first.

Formula:

\[ 100 \cdot \left(1 - \frac{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}{\textrm{Number of words}}\right) \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Naturalness by Zipf's law
docs.text:
anyts.style_stats.calc_zipf_naturalness()

Computation of the naturalness by Zipf's law: the agreement of the frequencies of the most frequent words with the ideal distribution \(f_r = f_1 / r\), where \(r\) is the rank. The first rank is ideal by construction, and above \(f_1\) the ideal frequency falls below one, so the ranks run from 2 to \(R = \min(\textrm{top\_n}, V, f_1)\). Negative values are cut to 0; without ranks to compare - all the words hapaxes, one lexeme or top_n below 2 - the value is nan.

Formula:

\[ 100 \cdot \left(1 - \frac{1}{R - 1} \sum_{r=2}^{R} \frac{|r \cdot f_r - f_1|}{f_1}\right) \]

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words (NAUSEA_TOP_N) messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

A top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Keyword density
docs.text:
anyts.style_stats.calc_keyword_density()

Computation of the keyword density (Text.ru): the occurrences of every keyword per 100 words. A keyword of several words separated by spaces is a sequence of words whose occurrences may overlap; the words and the keywords are compared by their normalized forms, and the keywords of a set come in sorted order.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words keywords list[str] - Keywords or phrases normalize Callable[[str], str] str.lower Normalized form of a word and of a keyword

docs.title: Density of phrases
docs.text:
anyts.style_stats.calc_phrase_density()

Computation of the density of the phrases of a list: their occurrences (find_phrases) per 100 words. The hook expand spells the phrases out in the forms of the text - the forms of a verb, contractions - every variant with its phrase; so the style metrics count the compound prepositions and the cliches.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words phrases list[str] - Phrases, words separated by spaces expand Callable None Variants of the phrases in the text, by the words and the phrases normalize Callable str.lower Normalized form of a word

docs.title: Parenthetical expressions
docs.text:
anyts.style_stats.find_parentheticals(), anyts.style_stats.calc_parentheticals()

find_parentheticals(text, phrases=(), *, is_parenthetical=None, expand=None, normalize=str.lower) finds the parenthetical expressions of a text: the phrases of the list, spelled out by expand as in calc_phrase_density, and the single words accepted by is_parenthetical outside the phrases found. It returns their bounds as slices of the words, in order. StyleStats counts its parentheticals and finds their markers this way, with its hooks. Hooks that are not callable raise SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words phrases list[str] () Parenthetical phrases, words separated by spaces is_parenthetical Callable[[str], bool] None Whether a word is a parenthetical expression by itself; none by default expand Callable None Variants of the phrases in the forms of the text with the phrase of each; the phrases as they are by default normalize Callable[[str], str] str.lower Normalized form of a word and of a phrase

calc_parentheticals(text, phrases=(), *, is_parenthetical=None, expand=None, normalize=str.lower) gives the expressions of find_parentheticals with the same arguments per 100 words.

from anyts.style_stats import calc_academic_nausea, calc_keyword_density, calc_zipf_naturalness

docs.title: Syntactic statistics
docs.text: anyts.syntax_stats.SyntaxStats

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The syntactic statistics of a text by its dependency tree (Ivanov, Solnyshkina and Solovyev 2018): dependency distances, tree depth, leaves and subtrees, valency of the finite verbs, coordination chains, clauses, modifiers of a noun, participial clauses, passive, infinitives, negations, split predicates and the ratio of the nouns to the verbs. The data source is a Doc object of spaCy with a dependency parse. Punctuation, symbols and whitespace are no nodes of the tree, and the distances are counted in positions of words. The measures of a sentence (the longest dependency, the depth, the nodes per leaf) are averaged over the sentences; the constructions are given per sentence.

A source that is not a Doc raises SourceTypeError; a source without a dependency parse (relations and sentence boundaries), without lemmas when the class requires them, or without words raises SourceError.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text:
A language library subclasses SyntaxStats. The defaults read Universal Dependencies with its morphological features and the relations it shares with ClearNLP; the passive and its agent read the relations of both:

Hook Kind Description parse(source) method Doc of a source; by default the source itself, which must be a Doc; a library may parse a string is_clause_head(token) method Whether a word heads a clause; by default is_clause_head of the module with join_hyphens of the class and the hook is_infinitive_periphrasis is_infinitive_periphrasis(token) method Whether an infinitive under xcomp, or an infinitive conjunct, makes one predicate with its head, a modal or phasal verb (can leave, begins to leave); none by default is_subordinate_clause_head(token) method Whether a clause head heads a subordinate clause, asked only of the words of is_clause_head; by default is_subordinate_clause_head of the module over the hook is_clause_head is_participle_clause(token) method Whether a word heads a participial clause; by default a participle that is not the head of the sentence, has no auxiliary or copula and has a dependent (calc_valency) is_passive(token) method Whether a word is a passive verb form; by default is_passive of the module with join_hyphens of the class is_agentless(token) method Whether a passive form has no agent; by default the hook is_passive without an agent (has_agent of the module) is_negation(token) method Whether a word is a word of negation; by default Polarity=Neg or a word of negation_words, a conjunction excluded find_split_predicates(words) method Pairs of a light verb and the noun that carries its meaning (to make a decision); none by default negation_words class attribute Words of negation besides Polarity=Neg, in lower case; none by default join_hyphens class attribute Take a word the tokenizer split at its hyphens for one word, in the tree and in the default hooks requires_lemmas class attribute Whether the source must carry lemmas, for hooks that read them stats_desc, stats_headers class attributes Statistics of get_stats with their descriptions (SYNTAX_STATS_DESC by default), headers of the columns for print_stats messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

The subclass adds the statistics of the constructions of its language (chains of complements by calc_modifier_chains, its own clauses) in its constructor from sents, with its own stats_desc. A negation_words that is not a collection of strings raises SourceTypeError when the class is defined, and so does a parse that does not return a Doc when the statistics are computed.

from spacy.tokens import Doc

from anyts.syntax_stats import SyntaxStats

docs.title: Metric functions
docs.text:
anyts.syntax_stats

Functions over the dependency tree of a spaCy Doc, a Span or a list of tokens; its words are the tokens of anyts.utils.is_word. They use only what Universal Dependencies and the ClearNLP labels of the English models share: the head of a token, the relations cc, conj, parataxis, punct and aux, the subjects nsubj and csubj, the modifiers of a noun amod, det, nmod, nummod and acl, and the root; the copula cop of predicate_form exists in Universal Dependencies alone. Everything else is up to a language library.

docs.title: get_words
docs.text: get_words(tokens, join_hyphens=False) returns the words of a sequence of tokens in their order; with join_hyphens=True a word the tokenizer split at its hyphens is one word, given by its part that holds its relation, as with the dependents of get_children (governor in He is vice-governor), or by its first part when a hyphen holds it.

docs.title: Hyphenated words
docs.text: A tokenizer may split a word at its hyphens (well-known into well, -, known), and a parser then hangs every part on its own head. With join_hyphens=True the functions of the tree take a word whose parts anyts.utils.joins_previous joins for one word with its hyphens. A word holding the head of the sentence has no head; the head of another one is that of its part hanging outside it, the nearest to the root (a word rather than a hyphen when equal). The dependents of a word are the words whose head hangs on one of its tokens, each given by that part (or by its first part when it hangs by a hyphen); its subtree is the word and the words that hang on it, directly or through punctuation. So every word has one dependency and is the dependent of one word.

docs.title: is_root
docs.text: Checks whether a token is the head of its sentence: its head is the token itself.

docs.title: base_dep
docs.text: The relation of a token without its subtype, which Universal Dependencies separates by a colon: nsubj:pass gives nsubj, expl:pass gives expl.

docs.title: get_children, count_children, subtree_len
docs.text:
get_children(token, join_hyphens=False) returns the dependent words of a token, punctuation and whitespace left out; with join_hyphens=True, the dependents of the whole hyphenated word the token belongs to.

count_children(token, join_hyphens=False) counts the dependent words of a token.

subtree_len(token, join_hyphens=False) is the number of words in the subtree of a token: the token itself and all of its direct and indirect dependents.

docs.title: calc_dependency_distances
docs.text:
The dependency distances (Liu 2008): the distance between a word and its head in positions of words, punctuation left out, in the order of the words. The head of a sentence and a word whose head lies outside the sequence are skipped.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc/Span/list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one position

docs.title: calc_tree_depth
docs.text:
The depth of the dependency tree: the longest path from the head of a sentence to a leaf, in relations between words; the maximum for several sentences, 0 for a sentence of one word. With join_hyphens a hyphenated word is one word, and the words that hang on any of its parts are one level below it.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc/Span/list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

docs.title: predicate_form
docs.text:
predicate_form(token, auxiliary_form) gives the verb form of a predicate by the forms (VerbForm) of its auxiliaries and copulas (aux and cop with their subtypes, anyts.constants.AUXILIARY_DEPS), as Universal Dependencies annotates them. A finite auxiliary makes the predicate finite wherever it stands (had arrived, the German gekommen sein wird); otherwise the first auxiliary decides (to have gone is an infinitive, being chosen a gerund), and without auxiliaries the word itself. A past participle auxiliary counts as finite, since it follows a finite one the parser may attach to another word (had been chosen); a present participle (having eaten) does not. A ClearNLP parse has no copula relation: its copula heads the clause with its own form, and its passive auxiliary auxpass is not read. An auxiliary the model leaves without a form is read by the language hook auxiliary_form, which gives its form or an empty string to skip it; without the hook it is skipped. A word with no verb form gives an empty string; a hook that is not callable raises SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token auxiliary_form Callable[[Token], str] None Verb form of an auxiliary without VerbForm

Example

import spacy
from spacy.tokens import Doc
from anyts.syntax_stats import predicate_form

vocab = spacy.blank("en").vocab
doc = Doc(
    vocab,
    words=["She", "had", "been", "chosen"],
    heads=[3, 3, 3, 3],
    deps=["nsubj:pass", "aux", "aux:pass", "ROOT"],
    morphs=["Case=Nom", "VerbForm=Fin", "VerbForm=Part", "VerbForm=Part"],
)
predicate_form(doc[3])
# 'Fin'
# An auxiliary the model left without a form, read by the hook
doc = Doc(
    vocab,
    words=["to", "have", "gone"],
    heads=[2, 2, 2],
    deps=["mark", "aux", "ROOT"],
    morphs=["", "", "VerbForm=Part"],
)
predicate_form(doc[2]), predicate_form(doc[2], lambda aux: "Inf" if aux.lower_ == "have" else "")
# ('Part', 'Inf')

docs.title: calc_valency
docs.text: The valency of a token: the number of its dependent words, the relations cc, conj, parataxis and punct left out (anyts.constants.VALENCY_IGNORED_DEPS); calc_valency(token, join_hyphens=True) counts a hyphenated dependent once, so came in Some-one came has one dependent and not two.

docs.title: calc_coordination_chains
docs.text:
The lengths of the coordination chains, in the order of their first words. A chain is a group of words linked by conj, whichever word each conjunct hangs on: Universal Dependencies attaches every conjunct to the first one (pears → apples, plums → apples), ClearNLP to the previous one (pears → apples, plums → pears); both give one chain of three for apples, pears and plums. A nested coordination (cats and dogs, or birds) and an enumeration split between several heads are one chain too. The length of a chain is the number of its words; a conjunct whose head lies outside the sequence is not linked to it. With join_hyphens a hyphenated word is one conjunct, linked by the conj of any of its parts (member and vice-governor is a chain of two).

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc/Span/list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

docs.title: is_predicate
docs.text: is_predicate(token, join_hyphens=False) checks whether a word can be the predicate of its clause: a verb (VERB, AUX) or a word with a subject of its own (nsubj, csubj and their subtypes, anyts.constants.SUBJECT_DEPS), so the nominal predicate of he is tall passes and a parenthetical word does not.

docs.title: Clauses and passive
docs.text:
anyts.syntax_stats.is_clause_head(), anyts.syntax_stats.is_infinitive_clause(), anyts.syntax_stats.is_subordinate_clause_head(), anyts.syntax_stats.is_passive(), anyts.syntax_stats.has_agent(), anyts.syntax_stats.is_agentless()

is_clause_head(token, join_hyphens=False, is_infinitive_periphrasis=None) checks whether a word heads a clause: the head of the sentence or a word with ccomp, advcl, acl, csubj or parataxis (anyts.constants.CLAUSE_DEPS, subtypes included) whose predicate (predicate_form, so has been built is finite) is not a participle, a converb or a gerund (NONFINITE_CLAUSE_FORMS, counted apart), nor an infinitive under acl; under xcomp, a finite predicate or an infinitive clause (is_infinitive_clause). A parataxis and a conjunct of a clause head count only as predicates (is_predicate); an infinitive conjunct is no clause by the check is_infinitive_periphrasis, since a model may attach the infinitive of a periphrasis to its verb as conj; a loop of conjuncts is no clause. A check of a periphrasis that is not callable raises SourceTypeError.

is_infinitive_clause(token, is_infinitive_periphrasis=None, is_clause_head=is_clause_head) checks whether an infinitive complement heads a clause of its own: an infinitive (predicate_form, so to be chosen is one) under xcomp (wants to leave), unless the language check is_infinitive_periphrasis says it makes one predicate with its head (can leave, begins to leave), or the word it completes, the first one up its chain of non-finite complements under xcomp (kept trying to leave, seemed able to leave), heads no clause by the check is_clause_head: an infinitive in a participial phrase or under an infinitive under acl (trying to leave, the wish to try to leave) belongs to that phrase. A ClearNLP parse hangs an infinitive after a predicative adjective on an acomp or oprd (is ready to leave), which heads no clause, so that infinitive is none. A check that is not callable raises SourceTypeError.

is_subordinate_clause_head(token, is_clause_head=is_clause_head) checks whether a word heads a subordinate clause: a clause head by the check is_clause_head with ccomp, advcl, acl or csubj (SUBORDINATE_CLAUSE_DEPS) or xcomp, or a conjunct of one, by the relation of the first word up its chain of conjuncts. A check that is not callable raises SourceTypeError.

is_passive(token, join_hyphens=False) checks whether a word is a passive verb form: a verb with Voice=Pass or a dependent nsubj:pass, csubj:pass, aux:pass, or nsubjpass, csubjpass, auxpass of ClearNLP (PASSIVE_DEPS).

has_agent(token, join_hyphens=False) checks whether a word has an agent: a dependent obl:agent, or agent of ClearNLP (AGENT_DEPS).

is_agentless(token, join_hyphens=False) checks whether a word is a passive form (is_passive) without an agent (has_agent).

docs.title: Noun phrases
docs.text:
count_noun_modifiers(token, join_hyphens=False) counts the modifiers of a noun phrase: the dependents with the relations amod, det, nmod, nummod, acl and their subtypes (anyts.constants.NOUN_MODIFIER_DEPS); conj and appos are no modifiers.

The lengths of the chains of nested modifiers, in the order of the words. A chain is two or more modifiers each hanging on the previous one, such as the complements of the increase of the efficiency of the use of resources (length 3); the check is_modifier of a language says what a modifier is (a complement with a preposition, a noun in the genitive). A chain starts at a modifier whose head is none, and its length is the number of modifiers in its longest branch. The links are those of get_children: punctuation is no link, and with join_hyphens a hyphenated word is one link. A check that is not callable raises SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc/Span/list[Token] - Sequence of tokens is_modifier Callable[[Token], bool] - Whether a word is a modifier of the chain join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

Example

import spacy
from spacy.tokens import Doc
from anyts.syntax_stats import calc_modifier_chains

doc = Doc(
    spacy.blank("en").vocab,
    words=["the", "use", "of", "the", "water", "of", "the", "river"],
    heads=[1, 1, 4, 4, 1, 7, 7, 4],
    deps=["det", "ROOT", "case", "det", "nmod", "case", "det", "nmod"],
)
calc_modifier_chains(doc, lambda token: token.dep_ == "nmod")
# [2]

docs.text:
anyts.utils

Input checks shared by the functions and classes of the core; their messages are in English.

docs.title: check_sequence
docs.text:
Checks that an argument is a sequence and not a text or an iterator. A string (of characters or bytes), a Doc, a Span, an iterator, an object that cannot be iterated or has no length, and a table - a two-dimensional array or a DataFrame - raise SourceTypeError: a string would be iterated by characters, and an iterator exhausted by the first pass. A set or a mapping holds every item once, in no order of the text, and raises the error too unless ordered=False, for a collection such as stop words.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check what str "words" What is expected, for the message of the error ordered bool True Whether the order and the repeats of the items matter

docs.title: check_words
docs.text:
Checks that an argument is a list of words: it passes check_sequence and every item is a string, so a list of spaCy tokens raises SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description value Iterable - Value to check what str "words" What is expected, for the message of the error ordered bool True Whether the order and the repeats of the words matter

docs.title: check_word
docs.text:
Checks that an argument of a function of a single word, such as the syllables of a language, is a word: a value that is not a string raises SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check what str "word" What is expected, for the message of the error

docs.title: check_counts
docs.text:
Checks that an argument is a counter - a mapping of words to their frequencies, such as a Counter: a value that is not a mapping, a word that is not a string or a frequency that is not a number raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite frequency SourceError.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check

docs.title: check_integer
docs.text:
Checks that a parameter is an integer: a bool or a float, even a whole one like 5.0, raises ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check what str - Name of the parameter, for the message of the error

docs.title: check_number
docs.text:
Checks that a parameter is a finite real number: a bool, a string, None, nan or an infinity raises ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check what str - Name of the parameter, for the message of the error

docs.title: check_callable
docs.text:
Checks that an argument is a function, such as a hook a function of the core takes as a parameter: a value that cannot be called raises SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check what str - Name of the argument, for the message of the error

docs.title: Collections and phrases
docs.text:
anyts.utils

A fixed order of a collection, the search of phrases in a list of words and the counts of the words of spans.

docs.title: in_order
docs.text: in_order(words) puts a collection of words in a fixed order: a list keeps its order, a set or a mapping is sorted.

docs.title: find_phrases
docs.text:
Finds phrases in a sequence of words and gives their bounds as slices of the words, in order. The words and the phrases are compared by their normalized forms, the lower case by default; at every position the longest phrase is taken, the phrases found do not overlap, and empty phrases are skipped. Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text phrases list[str] - Phrases, words separated by spaces normalize Callable str.lower Normalized form of a word and of a phrase

Example

from anyts.utils import find_phrases

find_phrases(["In", "fact", "it", "rains"], ["in fact", "in"])
# [(0, 2)]

docs.title: count_words_by_spans
docs.text:
Counts the words in every span of a text - a sentence, say - by the positions of the first characters of the words and the bounds of the spans, both in order. A word belongs to the span of its first character, and a span without words is skipped. Positions or spans that are not a sequence raise SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description starts list[int] - Positions of the first characters of the words spans list[tuple[int, int]] - Spans: the start and the position after the end

Example

from anyts.utils import count_words_by_spans

count_words_by_spans([0, 4, 10, 14, 20], [(0, 9), (9, 10), (10, 19), (20, 24)])
# [2, 2, 1]

docs.title: Labels and messages
docs.text:
anyts.utils

The labels of the plots and the messages of the errors that a language library passes over the English defaults.

docs.title: merge_labels
docs.text:
Merges the labels given for a plot over its default ones; a label not given keeps its default. A default with fields in braces, such as "Moving average ({window})", is a format string: a label given for it may use only those fields, with a literal brace doubled ({{), and is tried on sample values of the fields, so that a format spec the values do not take ({window:s} for a number) fails before a figure is created. The other labels are taken as they are. Labels that are not a mapping of strings, or have an unknown key, a field their default lacks or a format spec their values do not take, raise ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description defaults dict[str, str] - Default labels by key labels dict[str, str] - Labels given; None - the default ones **samples object - Values of the fields of the format labels, for trying the labels given

The defaults of the visualizers of the core are anyts.constants.VISUALIZER_LABELS, by the name of the function.

Example

from anyts.utils import merge_labels

merge_labels({"title": "Plot", "xlabel": "x"}, {"title": "My plot"})
# {'title': 'My plot', 'xlabel': 'x'}

docs.title: check_messages
docs.text:
Checks the messages of the errors a class of statistics raises: they must be complete, a string for every key of the defaults, so that an error never turns into a KeyError, and a message whose default has fields in braces may use only those fields, with a literal brace doubled ({{). The classes of statistics check the messages of a subclass when it is defined. Messages that are not a mapping of strings, lack a key, have an unknown one or a field their default lacks raise ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description messages dict[str, str] - Messages by key defaults dict[str, str] MESSAGES Default messages by key

docs.title: spaCy objects
docs.text:
anyts.utils

Checks of spaCy objects without importing spaCy, the words of a Doc and their morphology, the parts of a hyphenated word, the sentences of a Doc and the tokenizer rules of a language.

docs.title: is_doc, is_span
docs.text:
is_doc(value) checks whether a value is a Doc object of spaCy without importing spaCy: such an object exists only once spaCy is loaded, so before that every value gives False. A library checks its sources this way to keep its import free of spaCy.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check

is_span(value) checks whether a value is a Span object of spaCy, without importing spaCy as is_doc.

Example

import spacy
from anyts.utils import is_doc, is_span

doc = spacy.blank("en")("The cat sleeps")
is_doc(doc), is_doc(doc[:2]), is_span(doc[:2]), is_doc("The cat sleeps")
# (True, False, True, False)

docs.title: has_sents
docs.text:
Checks whether a Doc has its sentence boundaries: they count when every token has them, as after the parser, senter or sentencizer. The starts of a component that leaves the other tokens unset, such as start_sents_after_blank_lines without the parser, are partial; the statistics, kwic, sentence_lengths and the highlighting take the sentences of such a Doc from its text.

Parameter Type Default Description doc Doc - Doc object

Example

import spacy
from anyts.components import start_sents_after_blank_lines
from anyts.utils import has_sents

nlp = spacy.blank("xx")
text = "Notes\n\nThe cat sleeps. The dog eats."
doc = start_sents_after_blank_lines(nlp(text))
doc.has_annotation("SENT_START"), has_sents(doc)
# (True, False)
nlp.add_pipe("sentencizer")
has_sents(nlp(text))
# True

docs.title: is_word
docs.text: Checks whether a token is a word: not whitespace and not a token of is_punctuation, so symbols like %, €, + and invisible characters are no words either. The words of iter_doc_tokens and the nodes of the dependency tree of the syntactic statistics are such tokens.

docs.title: has_feature
docs.text:
Checks whether a token carries a morphological feature with a given value: has_feature(token, "VerbForm", "Fin").

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token field str - Name of the feature value str - Value of the feature

docs.title: Verb forms
docs.text:
is_finite_verb(token) checks whether a token is a finite verb: the part of speech VERB with VerbForm=Fin, so a finite auxiliary (AUX) is not one.

is_infinitive(token) checks whether a token is an infinitive, VerbForm=Inf whatever its part of speech.

docs.title: joins_previous
docs.text: joins_previous(token) checks whether a token continues a word the tokenizer split at its hyphens (well-known into well, -, known): the token is a word right after a hyphen that follows a word, with no whitespace around the hyphen and no sentence starting at the hyphen or the token. iter_doc_units and the functions of the dependency tree join the parts of a word by this rule with join_hyphens=True.

docs.title: iter_doc_tokens
docs.text:
Yields the tokens of the words of a Doc or a Span (is_word): whitespace tokens and the tokens of is_punctuation, symbols like % and € included, are skipped.

Parameter Type Default Description source Doc/Span - Doc or Span object

docs.title: iter_doc_units
docs.text:
Yields the words of a Doc or a Span as lists of tokens: one token each, as in iter_doc_tokens. With join_hyphens=True a word that the tokenizer split at its hyphens (well-known into well, -, known) is joined back by the rule of joins_previous; a language library whose tokenizer keeps such words whole turns it on, so that a string and a Doc give the same words.

Parameter Type Default Description source Doc/Span - Doc or Span object join_hyphens bool False Join the parts of hyphenated words

docs.title: iter_doc_words
docs.text:
Yields the words of iter_doc_units as tuples: the position of the first character, the position after the last character and the text of the word. A byte order mark glued to the start of a word, as in a file read with utf-8 instead of utf-8-sig, is dropped.

Parameter Type Default Description source Doc/Span - Doc or Span object join_hyphens bool False Join the parts of hyphenated words

Example

import spacy

from anyts.utils import iter_doc_words

doc = spacy.blank("xx")("A well-known cat")
[word for _, _, word in iter_doc_words(doc)]
# ['A', 'well', 'known', 'cat']
list(iter_doc_words(doc, join_hyphens=True))
# [(0, 1, 'A'), (2, 12, 'well-known'), (13, 16, 'cat')]

docs.title: split_doc_units
docs.text:
Splits the words of a Doc or a Span into the sentences of a sentence extractor, for a Doc without sentence boundaries or one to split otherwise: the sentences are found in its text in their order, and a word of iter_doc_units belongs to the sentence its first token lies in. The words outside the sentences found, those the extractor drops, are left out, so no sentence found gives no words.

Parameter Type Default Description source Doc/Span - Doc or Span object sents_extractor SentsExtractor - Sentence extraction tool join_hyphens bool False Join the parts of hyphenated words

docs.title: add_tokenizer_rules
docs.text:
Adds the rules of a language to the tokenizer of a pipeline, so that the tokens of a Doc match the words a library splits a string into. The prefixes (such as the dashes of a dialogue glued to a word), suffixes and infixes are regular expressions joined to those of the tokenizer, every branch of a prefix anchored at the start and of a suffix at the end. An abbreviation becomes a single token in lower case, capitalized and in upper case when the tokenizer keeps one of its forms whole. A rule the tokenizer already has as a top-level alternative is not added twice; a tokenizer that is not the Tokenizer of spaCy, or whose rules are not regular expressions, is left as it is. A rule is joined to others, so it sets its flags in a group, (?i:...). Rules that are not lists of strings and abbreviations that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, a rule that is not such a regular expression ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description nlp Language - Pipeline whose tokenizer gets the rules prefixes list[str] () Patterns of the prefixes, without the anchor suffixes list[str] () Patterns of the suffixes, without the anchor infixes list[str] () Patterns of the infixes abbreviations list[str]/set[str] () Abbreviations in lower case

Example

import spacy
from anyts.utils import add_tokenizer_rules

nlp = spacy.blank("en")
add_tokenizer_rules(nlp, prefixes=[r"-{2,}(?=\w)"])
[token.text for token in nlp("--No, he said.")]
# ['--', 'No', ',', 'he', 'said', '.']

docs.title: Words and tokens
docs.text:
anyts.utils

Checks of the words of a text and the counts of their letters.

docs.title: is_punctuation
docs.text:
Checks whether a token consists only of punctuation marks and symbols: the characters of the Unicode categories P (punctuation), S (symbols), M (combining marks) and Cf (invisible format characters such as the zero-width space U+200B, the byte order mark U+FEFF and the zero-width joiner U+200D). So ?!, --, €, №, a lone invisible character and an empty token are punctuation, and a token with a letter or a digit is not (e with a combining acute accent is a word). The results are cached by token, so the function is meant for tokens, not whole texts.

Parameter Type Default Description token str - Token

Example

from anyts.utils import is_punctuation

is_punctuation("?!"), is_punctuation("€"), is_punctuation("no.")
# (True, True, False)

docs.title: is_number
docs.text: is_number(word, pattern) checks whether a word is a number by a pattern matched against the whole lower-cased word, NUMBER_PATTERN by default, the numbers of WordsExtractor; a language passes its own (ordinals, Roman numerals).

docs.title: count_letters
docs.text:
Counts the letters of a word: the characters of any alphabet (str.isalpha), without digits, hyphens and marks. The results are cached by word form, so the function is meant for words, not whole texts.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word form

Example

from anyts.utils import count_letters

count_letters("well-known"), count_letters("3rd")
# (9, 2)

docs.title: has_words
docs.text:
Checks whether a text, a Doc or a Span holds a word: an empty text or one of whitespace and the characters of is_punctuation alone holds none.

Parameter Type Default Description source str/Doc/Span - Text, Doc or Span object

Example

from anyts.utils import has_words

has_words("The cat sleeps"), has_words("?!"), has_words("")
# (True, False, False)

docs.title: Corpus plots
docs.text: anyts.visualizers.dispersion_plot(), anyts.visualizers.keyness_plot(), anyts.visualizers.collocation_network()

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Plots for the corpus measures: the lexical dispersion (where in a text a word occurs), a chart of the keywords of keyness and a network of the collocations of collocations. The matplotlib functions take the axes ax, a new figure without them, and return Axes; the network is a graphviz Graph, as the word tree is a Digraph.

docs.title: Lexical dispersion
docs.text:
A row for every word of targets and a tick at the position of each of its occurrences in the text. Words are compared as they are: case and lemmatization belong to the extraction of the words.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order targets list[str] - Words whose occurrences are shown ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel

Words or targets that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, no words or no targets SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Chart of keywords
docs.text:
Diverging horizontal bars: the words of positive to the right, of negative (the result of keyness with positive=False) to the left, top_n on each side. The length of a bar is the absolute value of the field (score, g2, log_ratio), so the side is set by the list, not by the sign of the measure; words with an undefined or infinite value are skipped. For the odds ratio (from 0 to infinity, one - equal odds) log=True plots the absolute \(\log_2\) of the value, symmetric around one.

Parameter Type Default Description positive list[Keyword] - Positive keywords negative list[Keyword] () Negative keywords top_n int 20 Number of words on each side labels dict[str, str]/tuple[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel and xlabel_log (format strings with field), target and reference (the legend); a pair of strings sets the legend alone field str score Field of Keyword whose values are plotted log bool False Plot \(\log_2\) of the value - for the odds ratio ax Axes None Axes for the plot

Keywords that are not a list raise SourceTypeError, and no keyword with a finite value SourceError. An unknown field, a top_n that is not an integer of at least one, labels that merge_labels refuses or a legend that is not a pair, and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Network of collocations
docs.text:
An undirected graph in the neato layout: the nodes are the words, the size of the font by frequency, the edges the pairs, the width and the label by the measure. A pair of a word with itself (a word repeated within the window) would be a loop and is left out before top_n. Rendering needs the executables of Graphviz; Jupyter displays the graph, and graph.render("network") saves a png file.

Parameter Type Default Description collocations list[Collocation] - Collocations top_n int None Number of pairs from the start of the list; None - all of them

Collocations that are not a list raise SourceTypeError, no pair of two different words SourceError, and a top_n that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

from anyts.corpus import collocations, keyness
from anyts.visualizers import collocation_network, dispersion_plot, keyness_plot

target = "the cat sleeps and the cat eats and the cat purrs".split()
reference = "the dog sleeps and the dog eats and the dog barks".split()
dispersion_plot(target, ["cat", "eats"])
keyness_plot(keyness(target, reference), keyness(target, reference, positive=False))
print(collocation_network(collocations(target, window=1)).source)

docs.title: Literature fingerprinting
docs.text: anyts.visualizers.fingerprinting()

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Visualization of literature fingerprinting (Keim and Oelke 2007).

Every text is cut into segments of segment_len words with a sliding step of a tenth of a segment, and a measure of lexical diversity is computed for every segment. All segments are segment_len words long, so the values are comparable: when the step leaves words after the last segment, one more ends with the text, and a text not longer than a segment is one segment.

A text is a block of squares, its segments row by row, 8 rows high, or one column with at most 8 segments; a block wider than the drawing area wraps into rows of that width. The blocks go left to right and wrap within an area 2 · x_size wide, which grows downwards from 2 · y_size when they need more height. The colorbar runs from the smallest to the greatest finite value over all the texts; undefined values (nan on segments too short for the measure) and the empty cells of a block are light grey, unlike any value, zero included. A list without texts or a text without words raises SourceError.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description texts list[list[str]] - List of lists of words segment_len int 10 Size of a segment metric Callable None Function of a measure of lexical diversity; calc_ttr by default x_size int 800 Half the width of the drawing area, greater than 25 (the margin between the blocks) y_size int 600 Half the height of the drawing area, which grows when the blocks need more cmap str 'viridis' Colour map ax Axes None Axes of matplotlib for the plot; if not given, a 15×10 figure is created labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title

The function returns the Axes with the visualization, set to an equal aspect so the squares stay square; the figure is ax.figure. Texts that are not a list of lists of strings and a metric that cannot be called raise SourceTypeError. A segment_len or a y_size that is not an integer above zero, an x_size that is not an integer above 25, an unknown cmap, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

from anyts.diversity_stats import calc_mattr
from anyts.visualizers import fingerprinting

texts = [
    ("the cat sat on the mat " * 20).split(),
    " ".join(f"word{index % 37}" for index in range(150)).split(),
]
fingerprinting(texts, segment_len=20, metric=calc_mattr)

docs.title: Text highlighting
docs.text: anyts.visualizers.HighlightedText, anyts.visualizers.Highlight; the helpers of the layers are in anyts.visualizers.highlight

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Highlighting of a text by layers, in the manner of the style checkers: every layer marks the fragments of a text that a statistic counts - long sentences, complex words, the passive. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy. The result shows in Jupyter as HTML with styles and a legend; to_html returns the markup, and highlights keeps the fragments for a rendering of one's own. Fragments of different layers may overlap.

docs.title: Language hooks
docs.text:
The core has no layers of its own: a language library subclasses HighlightedText and sets its layers and their search.

Hook Kind Description layers_desc class attribute The layers in the order of drawing with their names in the legend, dict[str, str] default_layers class attribute The layers on by default, among those the source allows, tuple[str] layer_annotations class attribute The annotations of a Doc a layer needs (DEP, POS, LEMMA...), dict[str, tuple[str]]; a layer without them is available for a string too layer_styles class attribute The CSS declarations of every layer, dict[str, str]; the text of a layer with a background keeps a dark colour on it css_prefix class attribute The prefix of the CSS classes, str find(layer, words, sents, doc) method The fragments of a layer: a list of Highlight from the words and the sentences of the text and the Doc (None for a string) iter_words(text), iter_sents(text) methods The words and the sentences of a string as triples of the start, the end and the text; by default those of the default tokenizers of WordsExtractor and SentsExtractor doc_words(doc) method The words of a Doc; by default get_doc_words annotation_names class attribute Names of the annotations in the message of a layer a source does not allow, dict[str, str]; English by default messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

The sentences of a Doc come from its boundaries, or from iter_sents over its text when it has none or partial ones (has_sents). iter_sents gets the parts of a text between blank lines one by one, so a blank line always ends a sentence; a sentence holds the words of doc_words or iter_words that start in it. find runs in __init__: a subclass stores its own parameters, checked by check_params, before calling the __init__ of the base, and may find its layers with the finders of the layers. A fragment of another layer, an empty one or one outside the text raises ParameterError; a find that does not return Highlight objects, and an iter_words or an iter_sents whose triples are not ascending integer bounds inside the text with the text of each, SourceTypeError.

In the core the layers are empty and css_prefix is anyts.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str/Doc - Data source (a string or a Doc object) layers list[str]/str None Layers of the highlighting; if not given, the default layers the source allows; "all" - every layer allowed

A source that is neither a string nor a Doc raises SourceTypeError, a source without words SourceError; layers that are not a name or a list of names, a layer that is unknown or one that needs an annotation the source lacks raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description text str Text of the data source layers tuple[str] Layers turned on, in the order of drawing highlights tuple[Highlight] Highlighted fragments, sorted by their start and then by descending end counts dict[str, int] Number of fragments of every layer

A Highlight fragment is an immutable object with the fields start and end (positions in the text), layer (the layer) and note (the explanation for the tooltip).

docs.title: to_html
docs.text:
Returns the HTML markup of the highlighted text: a div of the class <prefix>-highlight with the legend, its counts and the text, where a highlighted segment is a span of the classes <prefix>-hl and <prefix>-hl-<layer> with the notes in its title; <prefix> is css_prefix. Overlapping fragments of different layers give segments with several classes, in the order of drawing. Line breaks (\n, \r\n, \r) become character references, one per break, so the markup can go into Markdown.

Parameter Type Default Description legend bool True Add the legend with the counts of the fragments css bool True Add the styles of the layers

docs.title: css
docs.text: The class method css() returns the styles to_html adds: the container, the legend and the text under the classes of css_prefix, the declarations of layer_styles for every layer, and a dark colour of the text on the layers with a background.

docs.title: Helpers of the layers
docs.text:
Word(start, end, text, pos=None, lemma=None) - a word with its position in the text and, when known, its part of speech and lemma.

Sent(start, end, n_words) - a sentence with its position and number of words.

get_doc_words(doc) - the words of iter_doc_tokens with their positions, a byte order mark at the start of the text left out, with the part of speech and the lemma when the Doc has them.

iter_doc_sents(doc) - the sentences of the boundaries of a Doc as triples of the start, the end and the text; the whitespace tokens at the edges of a sentence are left out, and a sentence of whitespace alone is skipped.

get_text_sents(spans, words) - the sentences given by their positions with their numbers of words; a word belongs to the sentence of its first character.

group_words_by_sents(words, sents) - the words of every sentence; the words out of the sentences are skipped.

tokens_span(tokens) - the positions of the fragment that covers some tokens, without the punctuation and the whitespace at its edges.

split_segments(length, highlights) - the segments of a text with the same set of fragments: their bounds are the starts and the ends of all the fragments, and overlapping or nested fragments give segments with several layers.

docs.title: Finders of the layers
docs.text:
The layers the languages share are found by functions that take the language as parameters: the notes of the fragments (callables where they read a number, so a language writes its plural forms; English by default), the counts of syllables, the normalized forms of the words, the stems, the matcher of the connectors. A subclass calls them from its find. A value that cannot be called for a parameter that takes a function, such as count_syllables, normalize or stem, raises SourceTypeError.

find_long_sents(sents, long_sent_word_factor, note) - the layer long_sents: the sentences of that number of words or more, the note by their number of words. A long_sent_word_factor that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

find_complex_words(words, complex_syl_factor, count_syllables, note) - the layer complex_words: the words of that number of syllables of count_syllables or more, the note by their number of syllables. A complex_syl_factor that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

find_words(words, is_match, layer, note) - a layer of single words, such as stopwords, rare words or verbal nouns: the words of the check is_match of a language, with one note.

find_phrase_highlights(words, phrases, layer, note, normalize) - a layer of the phrases of a list, such as compound prepositions, clichés or parentheticals. The phrases are matched by the normalized forms of their words, each normalized alone as in the text (find_phrases). A mapping gives their variants - contractions, forms of verbs - with the phrase each stands for; of the variants that normalize alike the first wins. A set of phrases is read in order (in_order). A fragment spans the phrase in the text; its note reads the phrase of the list, in quotes by default. Phrases that are not a collection of strings or a mapping of strings raise SourceTypeError.

find_connector_highlights(words, sents, matcher, note, pos) - the layer connectors: the connectors of a ConnectorMatcher of the language inside every sentence, in the whole text when the sentences are None; a one-word connector is checked by its part of speech when a word of the sentence has one - its own, or that of the hook pos. The note gives the class and the kind of the connector by default.

find_split_predicate_highlights(pairs, note) - the layer split_predicates: a fragment for every pair of a light verb and its noun a language finds, from the first word of the pair to the last; the note reads their lemmas by default.

calc_alliteration_runs(words, frequencies, threshold, stem, is_transparent) - the runs of two or more neighbouring words with a consonant of frequencies in the stem of each (the stem of a language leaves out the endings that repeat by agreement) and a probability below the threshold (anyts.constants.ALLITERATION_THRESHOLD, 0.001). The probability under an independent spread of the consonants is the product over the words of \(1 - (1 - f)^n\), \(f\) the frequency of the consonant and \(n\) the length of the stem. A transparent word - by default one shorter than ALLITERATION_MIN_WORD_LEN (3) letters, a stopword for a language - neither breaks nor continues a run; the words are taken in lower case. Words that are not a list of strings and frequencies that are not a mapping of strings to numbers raise SourceTypeError, and a frequency outside [0, 1] or a threshold outside (0, 1] ParameterError.

find_alliteration(words, sents, frequencies, threshold, stem, is_transparent, note) - the layer alliteration: the runs of calc_alliteration_runs inside every sentence, in the whole text when the sentences are None, the note by the consonant. The frequencies and the threshold raise the errors of calc_alliteration_runs.

check_params(long_sent_word_factor, complex_syl_factor, alliteration_threshold, *, messages) checks the parameters of the highlighting: a number of words or syllables that is not an integer of at least one, or a threshold outside the interval (0, 1], raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
A layer of the long sentences in a subclass.

Example

from anyts.visualizers import Highlight, HighlightedText


class Highlighter(HighlightedText):
    layers_desc = {"long_sents": "long sentence"}
    default_layers = ("long_sents",)
    layer_styles = {"long_sents": "background: #fef9c3;"}
    css_prefix = "demo"

    def find(self, layer, words, sents, doc):
        return [
            Highlight(sent.start, sent.end, layer, f"{sent.n_words} words")
            for sent in sents
            if sent.n_words >= 8
        ]


ht = Highlighter("The cat sleeps. The dog barks at the cat that sleeps on the mat.")
ht.highlights
# (Highlight(start=16, end=64, layer='long_sents', note='11 words'),)
ht.to_html(legend=False, css=False)
# '<div class="demo-highlight"><div class="demo-highlight-text">The cat sleeps. <span class="demo-hl demo-hl-long_sents" title="11 words">The dog barks at the cat that sleeps on the mat.</span></div></div>'

docs.title: Sentence lengths
docs.text: anyts.visualizers.sentence_lengths_plot(), anyts.visualizers.sentence_lengths()

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The curve of the lengths of the sentences - the rhythm of a text: the length of every sentence in words, in order, the moving average over window sentences and an inset with the histogram of the lengths. Short and long sentences in turn are an editorial sign of a lively text, a flat curve of a monotonous one. The function takes the axes ax and returns Axes.

sentence_lengths(source) extracts the lengths: a string is split by the sentence and the word extractors, a Doc by its boundaries and iter_doc_words with join_hyphens, and a Doc without boundaries or with partial ones (has_sents) is counted as its text. Sentences without words are skipped. Ready lengths (non-negative integers in a sequence or an iterator) are used as they are; a table, a set, a mapping, bytes, a length that is not an integer and an extractor of another type raise SourceTypeError, a negative length SourceError.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str/Doc/Iterable[int] - Text, Doc object or lengths of the sentences (a list, a numpy array, a Series) window int 10 Window of the moving average in sentences inset bool True Show the inset with the histogram ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel, length (the curve), average (a format string with window), distribution (the inset) sents_extractor SentsExtractor None Extractor of the sentences of a string; the sentence extractor of the library by default words_extractor WordsExtractor None Extractor of the words of a sentence of a string; the word extractor of the library by default

The source and the extractors raise the errors of sentence_lengths, and no sentences raise SourceError; a window that is not an integer of at least one, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

The core functions also take join_hyphens, False by default, which joins the parts of hyphenated words of a Doc with sentence boundaries (iter_doc_words). The extractors of the core are SentsExtractor() and WordsExtractor().

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

from anyts.visualizers import sentence_lengths, sentence_lengths_plot

text = "The cat sleeps. Does the dog? It eats, she said. Then both of them went out."
sentence_lengths(text)
# [3, 3, 4, 6]
sentence_lengths_plot(text, window=2)

docs.title: Stylometric plots
docs.text: anyts.visualizers.dendrogram_plot(), anyts.visualizers.pca_plot(), anyts.visualizers.mds_plot(), anyts.visualizers.mendenhall_plot()

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Plots for stylometry: a dendrogram and the multidimensional scaling of the matrix of distances of delta, the principal components of the frequencies of the most frequent words and the Mendenhall curves of several texts. The functions take the axes ax and return Axes.

docs.title: Dendrogram
docs.text:
Hierarchical clustering by scipy.cluster.hierarchy over the matrix of distances between texts, Ward's method by default as in Evert et al. (2015); the leaves are labelled by the index of the matrix. The columns are taken in the order of the rows; other texts in the columns than in the rows, fewer than two texts, an infinite or negative distance, asymmetry or a distance on the diagonal raise SourceError before a figure is created. Distances that are not a DataFrame of numbers raise SourceTypeError; an unknown method, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description distances DataFrame - Symmetric matrix of distances with the names of the texts in the rows and the columns, in any order method str ward Method of scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage to join the clusters: single, complete, average, weighted, centroid, median or ward ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel

docs.title: Principal components
docs.text:
Principal component analysis of the z-scores of the relative frequencies of the most frequent units (frequency_table, z_scores): the texts on the plane of the first two components with their names, the shares of the explained variance in the labels of the axes.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel and ylabel (format strings with the explained share)

The corpus, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table, and fewer than three texts raise SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Multidimensional scaling
docs.text:
Classical multidimensional scaling (Torgerson 1952) of any matrix of distances: the two leading eigenvectors of the double-centred squared distances, so the distances between the points approximate those of the matrix. The columns are taken in the order of the rows; other texts in the columns than in the rows, fewer than two texts, an infinite or negative distance, asymmetry or a distance on the diagonal raise SourceError before a figure is created. Distances that are not a DataFrame of numbers raise SourceTypeError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description distances DataFrame - Symmetric matrix of distances with the names of the texts in the rows and the columns, in any order ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

docs.title: Mendenhall curves
docs.text:
The shares of the words by length in characters (mendenhall_curve) of every text on one plot; a length no word has is drawn at zero.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Words of the texts by the names of the texts ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

A corpus that is not a mapping of lists of strings raises SourceTypeError, no texts or a text without words SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from anyts.corpus import delta
from anyts.visualizers import dendrogram_plot, mds_plot, mendenhall_plot, pca_plot

corpus = {
    "A": "the cat sat on the mat and the cat slept".split(),
    "B": "a dog lay on a rug and a dog barked".split(),
    "C": "the cat and a dog sat on the rug".split(),
}
distances = delta(corpus, n_mfw=5)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 10))
dendrogram_plot(distances, ax=axes[0, 0])
mds_plot(distances, ax=axes[0, 1])
pca_plot(corpus, n_mfw=5, ax=axes[1, 0])
mendenhall_plot(corpus, ax=axes[1, 1])

docs.title: Vocabulary growth and frequency spectrum
docs.text: anyts.visualizers.heaps_plot(), anyts.visualizers.frequency_spectrum_plot()

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Two plots of the distribution of the words of a text that complement Zipf's law: the growth of the vocabulary with the length of the text by Heaps' law and the frequency spectrum - how many word types occur exactly once, twice, three times. The functions take the axes ax and return Axes.

docs.title: Heaps' law
docs.text:
The size of the vocabulary \(V\) after every word of the text and the fitted curve \(V(N) = K \cdot N^{\beta}\) of fit_heaps with its parameters in the legend; the curve depends on the order of the words.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel, growth (the curve), fit (a format string with k and beta)

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, fewer than two words SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Frequency spectrum
docs.text:
The number of word types \(V(m)\) that occur exactly \(m\) times (calc_frequency_spectrum) in logarithmic coordinates; the left edge is the hapaxes. The spectrum underlies the measures of diversity of Yule, Sichel, Michéa and Honoré, and its shape shows how far the vocabulary of the text is from being exhausted.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, no words SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from anyts import WordsExtractor
from anyts.visualizers import frequency_spectrum_plot, heaps_plot

text = "The cat sat on the mat and the dog sat on the rug, and the cat saw the dog."
words = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract(text)
fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.5))
heaps_plot(words, ax=left)
frequency_spectrum_plot(words, ax=right)

docs.title: Word tree
docs.text: anyts.visualizers.wordtree()

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Building a word tree of the contexts of a keyword: the N-grams of up to max_n words that start or end with the keyword are counted in every list of words, such as a sentence. Every level keeps the max_per_n most frequent N-grams that continue a kept shorter one, alphabetically when equal; they are joined into two trees, after the keyword and before it, the size of the font by frequency (Wattenberg and Viégas 2008). Rendering needs the executables of Graphviz.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description texts list[list[str]] - List of lists of words keyword str - Keyword whose contexts are shown max_n int 5 Largest size of the context max_per_n int 8 Largest number of examples for every size of the context **kwargs - - Drawing parameters: max_font_size (default 30), min_font_size (12), font_interp - a function of the relative frequency of a node (its frequency over the greatest one, in (0, 1]) giving the share of the range from min_font_size to max_font_size, from 0 to 1; the cube root by default

The function returns a Digraph of graphviz. Texts that are not a list of lists of strings and a keyword that is not a string raise SourceTypeError; no texts, or a keyword with no word next to it in any of them, SourceError; a max_n that is not an integer of at least 2 and a max_per_n that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

from anyts.visualizers import wordtree

sentences = [
    ["the", "cat", "sleeps"],
    ["the", "cat", "eats", "fish"],
    ["a", "black", "cat", "sleeps"],
]
tree = wordtree(sentences, "cat", max_n=3)
tree.render("wordtree")

docs.title: Zipf's law
docs.text: anyts.visualizers.zipf(), anyts.visualizers.zipf_theory()

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Plotting Zipf's law from a counter of the frequencies of words.

Definition

Zipf's law (the rank-frequency law) is an empirical regularity of the frequencies of words in a natural language: with the words of a language, or of a long enough text, ordered by descending frequency, the frequency of the n-th word is roughly inversely proportional to its rank n. The second most frequent word occurs about half as often as the first, the third a third as often, and so on.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description counter Counter - Counter of the frequencies of words num_words int None Number of the most frequent words num_labels int 10 Number of the words labelled on the plot log bool True Use a logarithmic scale show_theory bool False Plot the theoretical Zipf's law alpha float 1.5 Exponent α of the theoretical Zipf's law, greater than zero show_fit bool False Plot the Zipf-Mandelbrot fit \(f(r) = C / (r + q)^s\) of fit_zipf_mandelbrot ax Axes None Axes of matplotlib for the plot; if not given, a new figure is created labels dict[str, str] None Labels of the plot over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel, experimental and theoretical (the curves), fit (a format string with q and s)

The function returns the Axes with the plot; a num_words greater than the number of word types does not extend the curves beyond the data. A counter that is not a Counter of strings raises SourceTypeError, and an empty counter or a frequency that is not above zero SourceError. A num_words below one, a negative num_labels, with show_theory an exponent that is not a finite number above zero, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError. All of them are raised before a figure is created.

zipf_theory(size, num_ranks, alpha=1.5, ax=None, labels=None) plots the theoretical curve alone, \(f(r) = size \cdot r^{-\alpha}\) for the ranks from 1 to num_ranks; its label is the key theoretical. A size or an alpha that is not a finite number above zero, a num_ranks that is not an integer of at least one, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Example

from collections import Counter

from anyts import WordsExtractor
from anyts.visualizers import zipf

text = "The cat sat on the mat and the dog sat on the rug, and the cat saw the dog."
counts = Counter(WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract(text))
ax = zipf(counts, num_labels=5, show_fit=True, labels={"title": "Zipf's law of a sentence"})
ax.figure.savefig("zipf.png")
